pages.transcription:
Petropolis (Brazil) 34 Gonçalves Dias 1. II 1942 Dear Hannah & Manfred
Mail has been irregular last weeks owing to the Conference and the
extension of war, but I am writing without to expect your news. Our
life is not at all changed by the season in Petropolis; we see very few
people; only the summer time has made our house more vivid. The
wife of the workman who has a room next to us, has got a baby, we
have got a dog, the dog has got fleas, we are getting them from him
mixed with bites of mosquitos, spiders and other little animals and
two snakes have appeared in our garden (not dangerous ones as one
told us) so we have a good picture of the tropical summer and it is
visible on our skin especially Lotte's whom the animals are as
fond as she is of our doggy - all her suppressed mother-instincts
are heaped upon him. Her health is not yet as I would like it and
perhaps we will give her some liver-injections to regain the lost
weight - of all our losses this one affects me most. I suppose we
all feel not very happy in these times especially as is it to be
supposed that they will continue and a real bright peace time
(also social and personal peace) lies far ahead but on the other
hand we have resigned to so much that at least with our ex-
terior form of life we get accustomed to war, uncertainty and
isolation. My little book on Amerigo Vespucci will be sent to
you this month from my American publisher - I will remind
him to do so; it is no big work and I hope the autobiography
which shall be published first in the original in Sweden is more
personal. Next week we hope to get the decision if we can have the
bungalow for next term - we do not like to move and are already
accustomed to the neighbourhood; you know how important it is to
have kind reliable people and especially here where doors and windows
are open day and night. It is true we have no precious things but for
the people here everything even an old trousers are a treasure. Because
if I have spoken only of us, but you know that all our thoughts are
with you and Lotte will write you more. Everfor you all Stefan

pages.transcription:
34 Rua Gonçalves Dias                                Petropolis, Febr. 1st, 1942.

Dear Hanna & Manfred,
I have very little to write except a few annotations to
Stefan's letter. My health is not at all bad and I am sorry that what he
writes must give you that impression. I may have lost a kilo or so in weight,
but he is the only one to notice it and in a country at war I would still stand
out as being particularly well-fed. Anyhow, to give him pleasure, the doctor
will make me a few liver injections. - The asthma, too, has not at all been
bad recently and I even gave Stefan the pleasure of a few quiet nights. Since
we are in Petropolis, I have had but one attack and that one very slight, just
strong enought to get an injection and to allow myself the luxury of a day in
bed. - The flea-bites is what annoys me most at present. Since about a week
Plucky's ~~xxxxx~~ fleas have developed a tendency to change over to Stefan and me
and I seem to have a specially wonderful taste for them because I get ten bites
while Stefan gets one. I hope to dominate that invasion very soon, however,
and fortunately my maid is not one of these refined ones and I can talk and
ask her assistance freely without hesitating. -
Officially we are now in the middle of the season, but
it is not half as bad as we thought. Contrary to European summer resorts the
people do not go out much and if they do, they just drive from oneplace to the
other. If we went to the Casino or the one fashionable Café we would probably
meet everybody we ever met in Rio. But as we don't we do not see many more
people than during the quiet time. We have had a few new visitors lately and
met some nice and in Stefan's sense cultured Frenchman, but on the whole our
life continues as before.
One request for an hour's work, dear Hanna, when you
next are in Bath. Now and then Stefan gets not offers but enquiries about the
film rights of his older books, and as we have no documents at all here, I
would be very grateful if you could find the folder of film agreements - it
once was in my writing desk in the study and should be either a slim cardboard
folder or ~~xx~~ the folder enclosed with the big box for agreements in general -
and just make me a list of the film agreements there are, 1) name of the work,
2)name of the film company, 3)whether world or language rights, 4) - this the
most important - whether there is a time-limit for the duration of the agree-
ment. I hope this does not give you much work, as those agreements are not
very many, I should think about a dozen altogether.
As again a fortnight has passed without bringing a
letter from you, we are again expecting it impatiently and are carefully
watching the postman's round every day, just as carefully trying to explain
each other when he has passed without entering, why your letter may have been
delayed. In any case the best method to avoid long gaps between letters from
you would be, just as we usually do, to write frequently even if there is
little to tell.
We have better weather now and enjoy not to
watch the change between rain, mist and fog all day long. The Conference has
brought many and long newspaper articles, but on the whole no change at all
in the usual life. In a fortnight Rio will have its famous carneval, and
although we avoid on principle all festivities we will go to Rio for a day
to watch the Carneval of the people in the streets which is supposed to be
a unique spectacle.
I, too, have only written about ourselves. But what is
the good of writing questions, you know very well that every little detail,
however insignificant in itself, greatly interests us, especially me, and all
you have to do is to sit down and write.

Unfortunately, I never got Kormendis
letter. Give please Sircauen[?] and fredental
my kindest regards Stefan

                                            Fondest love
                                            Lotte

pages.transcription:
10. II 1942
C/O EDITORA GUANABARA
RIO DE JANEIRO

Dear H. & M. we have no news from you since ages but
we know, it is not your fault - also from
New York all mail is endlessly delayed, may be because the
Conference wanted all the avions or because there is now much more mail
to forward owing to the fact that all letters to the last neutral countries in
Europe go no more directly over to Lisbon but over U.S. So we have the
impression to be still more away from you than ever. How we would
like to have you here {rather for more time} for one day for you cannot imagine how beau-
tiful it is in the summer days, the air sunny and clear, the mountains
beautiful, the vegetation gorgeous, - all would be perfect without the
cloudy thoughts. We do quietly our work without to be very active, there
is something in the atmosphere which makes you lazy and also the
idea, that a book in those times of unimaginable decisions is but a
ridiculous trifle tampers the intensity. We prefer to think that one has
to enjoy these quiet, peaceful and beautiful days in a country which has
no restrictions as something we will later remember with envy and
regret, so we are not as eager as we should be and play more with
the little sweet dog than reasonable people would do in a normal time.
Now in the season we see some friends and next week we go down to
Rio for one day to see the popular carnival (not the fashionable one)
which is a unique thing on earth; one has of course some mixed feeling
to assist to such fantastic explosion of joy in a time where nearly
in the whole world explosions kill people but it would be stupid not
to assist such a unique spectacle (as we have been in no theatre, no con-
cert and nearly no cinema since half a year and more.) By your letters
only I remember that the house in Bath exists for myself here nearly
forgotten that we had once one: to forget by some things, to resign is now
the great art we have to learn for all imagination cannot visualize the
coming world. I wish you could see our quiet and peaceful life, the
heavs wonderfully the monotony of this existence and enjoys the beau-
tiful surroundings: our life would be rather sad in an Northamerican
village but here the eye enjoys even if the it looks up from a news-
papers the glorious nature. Pardon me, if I write only about us but we
have nothing to say about you as your letters have not yet reached us.
Will you be so kind to forward the inclosed letter to Leni Hermann

as I like to send her only a few words. I hope you are in best health and
Manfred has much to do. Yours ever Stefan

pages.transcription:
Petropolis, Febr. 10th, 1942.
Dear Hanna & Manfred,
Nearly a month has passed again without letter from you
or mother, and also from USA we have not had mail for almost a fortnight. So
we spend every morning between 11 and 12, sitting on the steps and watching
out for the postman - unfortunately in vain. There are many reasons for postal
delay and we explain them to each other, but this does not make us less impat-
ient. I hope you have not had the same experience but are in continuous contact
with Eva. I am longing to hear how you are, what you are doing, whether there
are any changes in your life, that is to say whether Manfred has found an X-job
or whether Hanna is working with Anna Freud or anything else, etc. etc.
and hardly less we like to know about all our friends and acquaintances. -
We have been slightly more busy seeing people these last weeks and rather
enjoyed it after four months of almost complete solitude. We have made the
acquaintance of a few more European couples, pleasant and cultured people,
and my poor maid even had to stand the extra strain and excitement of luncheon
guests - tea guests do not excite her any more, this has already become routine
work. Also the weather has been fine the last weeks, real summer weather, hot
during the day and cool at night, but nevertheless we have not yet managed to
attain our ambition: to get up at 6 or 7 like most Brazilians do, in order to
profit from the fine morning. Also our walks have been reduced lately on
account of the more frequent visitors and invitations, and our dog whom I
took to Rio the other day to have him trimmed and who now looks perfectly
ridiculous, is rather reproachful about this matter of going out only in the
evening. But it can't be helped, it is too hot for long walks in daytime,
and the dog is not allowed either in train or busses. I suppose these few
details give you an idea of our life which is more quiet even now during the
season than we had dared to hope. But I am convinced the steps up to our
house detain many potential visitors from just dropping in, and as we care-
fully avoid the two or three places where you can meet everybody we only meet
those people we really want to meet. Stefan was at the reception of the
prefeito of Petropolis the other day (by some mistake I was not invited too)
but it seems that he kept in a corner with a few friends and only learned by
the visitor's list in the newspaper later on, how many acquaintances he has
missed. - He continues working and so I am occupied too, but on a somewhat
reduced scale, in the morning we wait for the mail half of the time, in the
afternoon there are often visitors, sometimes also in the evening, and so I
am enjoying a half-holiday which I partly use for trying out some more cooking
recipes. Linzertorte I could not make yet as the stove is so bad that our
landlady even promised me a new one, but I am mentally ready for it, as well
as for knitting another jumper for Eva as soon as I have news from her that
the cardigan arrived and how it fits. You see I am falling more and more in
the mentality of those women ~~which~~ who once bored me to death, and I also
understand now the writers' wives who do not always want to listen to their
respective husbands' intelligent conversation but prefer to discuss women's
problems among themselves. I simply have to get rid of the such trifling
details like the one that my maid when she needed greaseproof paper for a
cake used the wrapping paper of a tilsit cheese, or that she uses the dog's
special comb for herself (fortunately they both are very clean) and other
interesting things, and I badly need someone to talk over dressproblems and
hairdresser and the many kinds of insects in the house and so on and so on.
So far I have not yet found the right woman for all this as most of our
European friends have no household of their own, and mostly the acquaintance
is so new that they prefer to talk or to listen to Stefan instead of small
talk. So I unload part of these problems on Stefan, who listens with great
patience and, as the conditions here are so totally different, even with
some interest. Therefore you need not pity me too much.
Please send this letter on to mother, she will see from this one
that I really have nothing special or interesting to tell, and I am waiting
to hear from her again to write her at length (as I did about three weeks
ago with an enclosure to brother Jan).
Love to all Lotte

{Marginalie links: Stefan wants me to inform you that we will keep this little house for the so-called winter here.}
pages.notes: Typoskript mit handschriftlicher Marginalie am linken Rand. Die Marginalie ist in der Handschrift von Lotte Zweig verfasst.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer.

c/o EDITORA GUANABARA
132, RUA OUVIDOR
RIO DE JANEIRO

PETROPOLIS, (BRASIL)
(34, RUA GONÇALVES DIAS)

Dearest Hanne, Going away like this my only wish is that you
may believe that it is the best thing for Stefan, suffering as
he did all these years with all those who suffer from the Nazi
domination, and for me, always ill with asthma. I wish we could
have done more for Eva personally, having her with us all the time,
but on the other hand it is my sincere conviction that it has
been better for Eva to be with Mrs. Schaeffers whose understanding,
love and way of education is so much similar to your own.
Having her with us, she would have felt our moods, been lonely
probably and have without doubt great difficulties adapting
herself in such completely different surroundings. On Mrs. Sch.
you may count, I am convinced, like on one of the family.
My sister-in-law will also look after Eva and maybe even offer
to take her herself or send Eva somewhere else. But I who know
you and your ideas, would advise you to leave Eva at Schaeffer's.
Let us hope it is not too long until you can take her home.
Many many thanks for all you have been to me
and forgive me for causing pain to you and Manfred. Believe
me it is best as we do it now.
Lotte

Dear Hannah and Manfred, you would understand us better had you seen how
Lotte suffered in the last months from her asthma and I for my part was oppressed by
our nomadic life which did not allow me to do my work efficiently. We liked this
country enormously but it was always a provisory life far from our home, our friends
and for me with sixty years the idea to wait still for years of this horrible time became
unbearable. Had Lottes health been better and had we could have Eva with us it would
have had seem to continue but living in thoughts always with the others far away and
without any hope to have the quiet life I was longing for and to see Lottes health restored
(the long injection-care did not help at all) we decided, bound in love, not to leave each
other. I feel responsibility against you and Lottes mother, and on the other hand you know
how perfect we two have lived together these years and that there was not a moment of
disagreement between us. Let us hope that you will see your daughter soon and she can
give you all the love you merit; I have written to my brother and I am sure they will
do all they can for her. Our devoted friend, my publisher Abrão Koogan will tell you
one day about our last hours and that our thoughts have always been with you. Stefan
pages.notes: Brief auf Briefpapier mit Briefkopf. Handschriftlich in violetter Tinte. Sehr gut lesbar.
Rückseite des Briefbogens, leer.

pages.transcription:
HOTEL UTAH
The Hotel Beautiful
GUY TOOMBES,
MANAGER

SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH
Liebe Frau Doktor, vielen Dank für Ihren
Brief! Sie stellen sich aber die Tätigkeit
einer Secretärin falsch vor. Sie meinen, sie
sitzt still im Hotel und klappert Briefe und
Telefoniert. völliger Irrtum – sie ist bei
allem dabei, macht alle Ausflüge und
Autofahrten mit, glänzt bei den Luncheons
und Dinners als europäische Culturdame,
heute wollte sie sogar hier im Radio spre-
chen und mit den Professoren der verschie-
denen Universitäten ist sie so intim, dass
Heiratsanträge zu befürchten sind. Sie
hat bereits vortrefflich gelernt, vor den
Leuten so zu tun, als ob sie literarisch
und künstlerisch furchtbar interessiert
wäre, ich muss aber zu ihrer Ehre sagen,

“SEE AMERICA FIRST”
pages.notes: Brief auf Hotelbriefpapier. Handschrift in violetter Tinte. Die Zeile 'Telefoniert' ist am Ende der Zeile 5 leicht abgeschnitten, aber lesbar.

pages.transcription:
dass sie auch gelernt hat, sehr gut zu packen,
Billette zu verwalten und (bis auf später
Aufstehen) ihren Reisemarschallsdienst vor-
trefflich zu versehen. Immerhin wird es
shön sein, in New York noch zehn Tage
ohne Räder unter den Betten zu schlafen
und mit Luxushotels sind wir wohl bis
zum nächsten Jahr gründlich eingedeckt.
Ich habe nur erfreuliche Bekannten, dass
ich mich auf London freue, aber ehrig
darauf, nicht ständig auf dem Präsen-
tierteller zu stehen, vierundzwanzig
Stunden am Tag bezaubernd sein zu
müssen und – last not least – auch
weiter zu arbeiten.
Hoffentlich überstehen Sie
die vielen familiären Invasionen,
ich fürchte nur, dass Ihnen nicht
einmal Reparationen an Daarbarheit
gezahlt werden dürften für deren Ein-
brich in Ihr häusliches Territorium. Mit
den schönsten Grüßen an all die Ihre
SZ.
pages.notes: Handschrift in violetter Tinte. 'Daarbarheit' ist eine ungewöhnliche Schreibweise, vermutlich 'Darbarkeit' oder 'Darbarkeit' gemeint, aber so transkribiert wie geschrieben.

objects.confidenceNotes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar. Die Handschrift ist flüssig und typisch für Stefan Zweig. Einzig das Wort 'Daarbarheit' ist orthographisch unklar, wurde aber buchstabengetreu transkribiert.

pages.transcription:
Liebe Hannah, es gab noch mehr zu tun als wir dachten: erstens jene
Überraschung mit dem Dach, die bald behoben sein wird, dann erfordert der
junge Mann den ich als Gärtner-Handyman engagierte, einige kleine Erläute-
rungen um ihm ein Zimmer zu equippieren; auch wird das {noch} allerdings seltener,
breppant[?] nur treppauf. Samstag hoffen wir, das Haus still zu haben, dann
ist uns noch die Rechnung zu bezahlen das Lotte ist eine hoffentlich gläubige
Hausbesitzerin und muss uns nolens volens zur Hausfrau ausbilden. Ich
habe das Gefühl, dass die Gelder jetzt gut geölt sind und alles smoothly
sich fortwursteln kann.
Dass die Kinder ein kaum sind ist - ehrlich - gar nicht bemerkbar oder
nur in angenehmen Sinn. Mit dem neuen dienstbaren Geist wird diese
Schwester entlastet sein - dies war meine größte Befürchtung, denn es gab
doch von morgens bis abends mit den Arbeitern ein ständiges hin und her.
Jetzt werden keine Installationen mehr gemacht, ausser dass ich für den
neuen Boy die alte Wasserleitung in Küche I an die Wasserleitung an-
allieren kann; warmes Wasser muss er sich eben in paar Krügen von der
Heizung heruntholen wie es die Menschheit bis vor etwa 50 Jahren mittler-
neufach getan hat (ich habe es in meiner Kindheit selbst noch gesehen/
die elektrischen Laurer sah ich nur in flüchtigen Fotos, ich glaub
sie werden uns ausgezeichnet passen.
Ich hoffe Du meinst es nicht ernst mit der angedrohten Durchschla-
tap. Mir bitte ich freute an deren Haus wollen wir sein - ein
liebes Gefühl des Angehörigen, wenn wir zwei es allein bewohnen sollten
und gar in einer solchen Zeit. Ich fürchte, Ihr werdet ein paar stille
und relativ wylon Tage auf paar hohen Touren dringend nötig
haben; pessimistisch, wie ich veranlagt bin, sehe ich gerade für
die nächste Zeit wirst Du voran und ich glaube, schon an wir
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig, violette Tinte. Die Lesbarkeit ist aufgrund der kursiven Handschrift an einigen Stellen erschwert.

pages.transcription:
hat die Atmosphäre London etwas depressives - schon ohne Telefon ist
man mehr bei sich selber. Das wäre schon etwas, wenn Du das Haus
nur mitleben wolltest, lange es Placherei war und nicht jetzt, da
es nüchtern beginnt, ein Refugium und ein Privatatorium zu werden!
Wenn ich Urlaubsreif bin - ich denke in den ersten Dezembertagen
- muss ich ja ohnehin noch einmal nach London und werde das tun,
was gestern deine Schwester bei dieser Tochter besorgte, - nämlich Dir
den Kopf waschen wegen ihrer absurden Einfälle, dass sie uns Den-
fer für störende Elemente sind.
Nun will Lotte Dir noch schreiben, sie geht eben ungeduldig,
weil sie - es ist schon 1/2 10 - in das Bett gehen will, nicht aber
um mit den Hühnern aufzustehen, die wir noch gar nicht haben;
leider war ihr so toricht, ihr Komplott zu leisten, indem das Bett
jetzt noch den fehlenden Stützpunkt erhielt. Wenn Ihr kommt wird
es Euch einmal zum Nachprobieren gleichen.
Herzlichst Euch aller

Stefan
Ich habe zwar schon separat geschrieben, will
aber den fehlenden Platz nicht verschwendet
sehen. Zu sagen ist aber nichts mehr ausser dass
der Boy mit den Huntley Mahagonikommoden und
einem eleganten Waschgeschirr, schwarz mit Blumen
und pot-de-chambre to match, ein herrliches Zim-
mer haben wird. Hans und Gärten erwarten ihn
schon ungeduldig, ebenso ungeduldig wie ich die
Selfridge Lieferung. Grüsse Manfred, Heiner und
Mr. Lee, von dem ein Verwandter im Jahre 1815 der
erste Rosemount-Besitzer war.
Lotte.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, Fortsetzung auf Seite 2. Der untere Teil ist von Lotte Zweig geschrieben.

objects.confidenceNotes: Die Handschrift ist sehr flüchtig und weist viele Abkürzungen sowie individuelle Schreibweisen auf. Einige Wörter (z.B. 'breppant', 'toricht') sind schwer zu entziffern.

pages.transcription:
c/o EDITORA GUANABARA
132, RUA OUVIDOR
RIO DE JANEIRO

21. II 1942

PETROPOLIS, (BRASIL)
(34, RUA GONÇALVES DIAS)

My dear Eva, you may imagine that the idea we
should not see you any more is a very hard one,
for you know how we liked you and also now I
have great confidence in you that you will not see
a want of love for you in our going away. But
we had a very bad time. Auntie Lotte suffered
from her asthma and I myself felt so down as
never; I am afraid the climat here has made
auntie Lottes astma so much worse and I for my
part saw that in my age I would not see a change
for a quid life. When I was young I liked nothing more
than to travel but you know how I ~~liked~~ my house
and my books and the good sitting-together with
you all - in my age one gets easily tired.
Now, dear Eva, I do not want to forget
us, but I hope you will not feel lonely. You have
in Mrs Shaeffer the best friend, you have your
comrades and your work, you have - what I
did not have - the chance to see a better world,
where one can remain together with those one loves
instead to be divided from them by land and seas.
You have the best father and the best mother you
can wish; the more you learn now, the more
happier you are, the more you will make them happy.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Briefpapier mit gedrucktem Briefkopf. Die Tinte ist violett.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through).

pages.transcription:
c/o EDITORA GUANABARA
132, RUA OUVIDOR
RIO DE JANEIRO

PETROPOLIS, (BRASIL)
(34, RUA GONÇALVES DIAS)

How would we have liked to accompany you in your de-
velopment, to see you in the College, in your first love, to
follow with pride your growing-up, but we have to
leave this to your parents and {have} passed only long hours
to dream this over.
I am convinced that Mrs Stefanie Zweig will look
after you. She had never the luck to have children
and I have the impression that she likes you very much;
it is a good felling for me to know that also somebody
of my family has love for you.
And now farewell. Give my best regards to Mr.
Shaeffer and my old friend Shaeffer; you have been
with my thoughts and my poor love {till} to the last
moment, your old uncle

Stefan


[...]

Darling Eva, How we would have loved to have you live with
us while you are separated from your parents, but this was
is a cruell thing for all of us and what we wish and would
like to do counts for nothing. The only way to get over
this is the hope for better times when the Nazis will have
been beaten, and I am sure you will in not too distant
future return home and have a happy life with mummy
and daddy. That we have to go away before was a hard
decision to take, and although we cannot explain it and
you must believe and always think that it is for the
best like this, instead of being sorry. Auntie Olga, I am
sure, will help you to understand what we say, and it is
a great consolation for us to know you with her.

Fondest love
auntie Lotte
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Briefpapier mit gedrucktem Briefkopf. Besteht aus zwei Teilen, die auf einem Blatt zusammengefügt sind.
Rückseite des dritten Blattes, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through).

objects.confidenceNotes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur. Die wenigen Korrekturen und Einfügungen sind eindeutig.

pages.transcription:
Liebe Hannah, es ist rührend wie du dich mit unsern An-
gelegenheiten beschäftigst. Ich möchte aber nicht, dass Frau
Kahn und du schon jetzt hinaufziehen; es geht immerhin schon
auf October, es kommen nach unseren tagelangen Sonnen-Tagen auch
Regenwochen kommen[?] und ich möchte nicht, dass Ihr Euch in-
stalliert, solange nicht regelrechte Heizung functioniert. Auch dann
ist es noch anfordernd genug, in einem Haus zu sein, wo von mor-
gens bis abends geklopft, gehämmert, geläutet und ferngeschraubt
wird, wo niemand für Milch, Brot, etc sorgt. Ich glaube, mit dem
Hinaufziehen auch nur einer Person muss gewartet werden, bis
die Heizung functioniert — ich möchte nicht fremden Doktoren
hier etwas zu verdienen geben. (Wofür haben wir denn hier im Haus
ein camp bed?)
Wooster scheint sehr anständig die Sache anzugehen, wir haben
nach meinen Plänen auch manches der Arbeit vereinfacht.
Der Strongroom unterbleibt, da wir eine Art Safe entfernt
haben, wo ich Documente ruhig feuersicher aufbewahren kann,
die alte Badezimmerleitung bleibt bestehen, so dass der obere
Stock gar keine Durchbrüche erfordert und meiner Meinung
nach in zwei Wochen oder drei völlig bewohnbar sein könnte
— die eigentliche Arbeit beschränkte ich dann auf das Parterre.
Deine liebe Gegenwart wäre mir natürlich besonders will-
kommen, weil du Blick & Interesse und wie ich hoffe etwas
Freude am Einrichten hast; Frau Kahn wäre {am besten}
von dem Punkte an, wo ein Teil des Hauses bewohnbar und beheiz-
bar ist, vorher sehe ich für sie keine rechte Mission und nur Gele-
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, violette Tinte. Die Seite endet mitten im Wort 'Gele-'. Die Fortsetzung befindet sich auf Seite 2.

pages.transcription:
genheit, einen kräftigen Schnupfen und eine Bestärkung ihrer ofen-
maligen Schwächen zu erreichen. Wenn du alle jeden Tag einmal
hinaufgehst und ihr ab und zu was das Wesentliche anzeigt werden
die Crux ist momentan die Nachbarsfrage oder zumindest ein
Charwoman. Die erste Combination — Polizist — ist gescheitert
und ich sehe (mit einigen leichten Pertochenwallen[?]) jetzt sollte ich
Trab, bei den Agenturen sich umzusehen. Inzwischen habe ich für
den Weinkeller gesorgt und alles denkbare vorbereitet.
Tausend Dank und alles Herzliche für Euch alle

Stefan

Liebe Hanna!                               Samstag, 23.9.
Wenn Du zu Beginn des Innenar-
beiten dabei sein willst, musst Du bald
kommen — gestern, während Huntleys Möbelwagen
noch vor der Tür standen, arbeiteten bereits drei
Maler im guest room daran, die Tapete abzu-
reissen und sie haben vor, möglichst viele Zim-
mer auf einmal zu machen. Die anderen Ar-
beiter für Heizung, Bad etc. können wahrscheinlich
erst Ende der Woche anfangen. — Du brauchst
Dich aber in keiner Weise zu eilen. Komm, so-
bald es Dir passt, Mitte oder Ende der Woche,
wir freuen uns beide auf Dich, wohnen kannst
Du hier, die camp-bed-Frage werden wir Deinen
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, violette Tinte. Die Seite enthält den Abschluss des ersten Briefteils und einen neuen Briefabschnitt (datiert 23.9.).

objects.confidenceNotes: Der Text ist gut lesbar, trotz der kursiven Handschrift. Einige Wörter wie 'Pertochenwallen' sind aufgrund der individuellen Handschrift unsicher.

pages.transcription:
Liebe Johanna, ich melde Dir, dass wir heute Sams
tag eingezogen sind und es war insoferne ein house
warning als das Haus wirklich warm nur behaglich
bleibt. Dagegen sind die letzten Arbeiter noch nicht ab-
gericht[?] sind aber nur für winzige Kleinigkeiten,
alles steht und liegt an seiner Stelle, wir feite[?]
abends sogar im grossen Bett. Den Kindern geht
es gut, die Clarzershnie[?] fatale ist gut überstanden,
die medizinische Untersuchung in der Schule; heute
habe ich, der Guardian, einen Ukas erlassen, dass
jedes von Ihnen fünf offengelassene Türen per
Woche rationiert {bekommt}, jeder Überverbrauch dagegen
unter grausame Strafen fällt.
Lotte wird Dir bald zugerendet und Du fast dann
über Nichtstun kaum zu klagen (hoffentlich auch
Manfred nicht.) Ich hoffe, Montag früh hier die
Arbeit wieder aufzunehmen, morgen Sonntag wird
von früh bis abends Daten geräumt und alles auf
Tip und Top gestellt. Herzliche Grüsse Euer
Ich würde gerne Dienstag kommen,
bin aber noch nicht ganz sicher,
ob alles so weit ist. Herzlichst Lotte.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief in violetter Tinte. Das Wort 'Clarzershnie' ist schwer lesbar, möglicherweise ein Eigenname oder eine spezifische Bezeichnung. 'feite' könnte 'feierten' bedeuten, ist aber unvollständig geschrieben.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer.

objects.confidenceNotes: Die Handschrift ist flüssig, aber einige Wörter (z.B. 'Clarzershnie', 'abgericht', 'feite') sind aufgrund der individuellen Schreibweise von Stefan Zweig schwer eindeutig zu identifizieren.

pages.transcription:
Liebe Hannah, ich wollte Dir nur mitteilen, dass Quittner heute
telephonisch das Eintreffen 49, HALLAM STREET,
der Certificate meldete. Ich LONDON, W. 1.
bin etwas melancholisch für Euch bei diesem Anlass, denn wo LANGHAM 3693.
ich Bürger bin wird kein Korb gewonnen, ich bin eine sehr
schlechte militärische Acquisition. Ich komme dann nächste Woche
(zu Anfang) mit Lotte nach London, um alles registrieren zu lassen
und den Pass anzufordern und hoffe auf Euren Gegenbesuch
am Donnerstag. Rastet Euch gut aus, wir werden unsere Nerven
noch ausgiebig benötigen in den nächsten Monaten und Jahren.
Deine Tochter liegt vergnügt zu Bett und hat
heute einen Schneefall versäumt - unsere armen Erdbeeren,
aber wie wird der Gärtner jubeln, der sie nicht einpflanzen
wollte! Victor f. ist gestern noch einmal operiert worden,
hoffentlich ist diese Episode dann abgeschlossen.
Gestern waren wir bei dem naughty play, aber
es war so grauenhaft wenn meine Landsleute einmal naughty
sein wollen, dass wir nach dem zweiten Akt flüchteten
Herzlichst Euch allen
Herzliche Grüsse Lotte. Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Briefpapier mit gedrucktem Briefkopf. Die Zeilenumbrüche im Textkörper wurden beibehalten. Der Briefkopf ist in den Text integriert, wie er auf dem Original erscheint.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer. Leichte Stockflecken erkennbar.

objects.confidenceNotes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar. Die Integration des Briefkopfes in den Textfluss auf Seite 1 entspricht der physischen Anordnung auf dem Papier.

pages.transcription:
Liebe Hannah, vielen Dank. Aber ein so teurer und
prachtvoller Teppich kommt trotz Deiner Empfehlung nicht
in Betracht. Solche Beträge will ich nicht „mit Füssen treten“.
Wichtiger als all dies ist das die Führung des Hauses jetzt
endlich in Gang kommt und ich endlich erlebe, dass alles
klaglos läuft ohne dass ich mich bekümmern muss, wie ein
Tisch gedeckt wird und die Centralheizung angelassen. Das
erste Gebot - Hannah kennen wir besser zu teilen -
ein simpler Tee meisterte daran, dass wir keine zweite Kanne
für heisses Wasser (zum Nachgiessen/heisse sind Abwarten der
ersten Tasse) haben, das hatte also in den Monaten seit
wir in Bath bin nicht die primitivste Handwerkszeug einer
feinfühlenden Nation vorbereitet hat (in Lansdown besah ich
nun einmal eine Woolworthtasse.) darum geht es mir -
nicht ob zwei Farbtöne von Holz besser oder aberher [?] zu-
sammenstimmen, sondern dass ich endlich die Sicherheit
habe, dass, wenn es läutet, die Tür aufgemacht wird und
wenn ein Gast {kommt}, ich mich nicht {um Haustechnisches} zu kümmern habe. Dass
Lotte lernt, einen Haushalt auf einem gewissen Niveau
klaglos und geräuschlos laufen zu lassen. Sie wendet dann
immer ein, sie hätte nicht gesehen, wie man einen Tisch
anständig deckt oder wie man in guten Händen serviere“ —
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief in violetter Tinte. Die Lesbarkeit ist gut, einige Wörter sind aufgrund der kursiven Handschrift leicht interpretativ (z.B. 'aberher').

pages.transcription:
darauf muss ich antworten: gerade das darf niemand {gleich} mer-
ken, dass sie nicht in grosser Gesellschaft verkehrt hat. Fran-boi-
ner hat es eben auch gelernt und man muss sich darum
kümmern — es genügt auch nicht, einmal (in vielen Jahren)
in zwei Monaten ins Dienstbotenbüro zu gehen, sondern man
muss jeden zweiten Tag gehen und drängen und fragen. Deine
Schwester hat das Beste, aber sie kann nicht, ermüdet und
rastet von diesen Arbeiten, kochen und aufräumen und
einkaufen und für die Kinder sorgen. Lotte muss sich ener-
gisch dafür sorgen, dass der Haushalt läuft ohne dass ich
etwas davon spüre und höre. Ich habe auch monatelang
mit einem ungeputzten Anzug und ebensolchen Schuhen
ohne den Schatten einer Bedienung abgefunden; aber jetzt
muss einmal mit den ewigen Provisorien Schluss gemacht
werden; wenn sie zurückkommt muss sie anders ein-
greifen und zugreifen: dies ist wichtiger als alle Anschaffungen.
Heute ein erster Trinkenfall - nachts tropfte
es nach einem Regenguss in mein Schlafzimmer. Sie hätten
auchneuer etwas am Dach beim Reparieren vergessen; ich
musste in aller Früh schon um Woolter trompeten
Alles Herzliche von Eurem

New York, 8.7.40.
Regards to all who write to me!
Dear Hanna,
I had nearly finished a letter to you announcing our
good arrival in the States when I heard that a Clipper is leaving
to-morrow so that I try to catch it still with this letter.
We have arrived yesterday afternoon after a long and
in the last days very agreable crossing, were met by Stefan's
brother, went in our old hotel, the Wyndham, had dinner with my
brother-in-law and afterwards went to see Huebsch and his wife
who are taking us to the World Fair to-night. To-day we went to
the shipping company and arranged pur departure for the 26th July
so that we would arrive in Rio on the 7th or 8th August. We in-
tend to stay in the Wyndham for a week - Stefan has only the wish
to work quietly in his room and as it is beginning to get warm and
probably soon very hot work will be the best thing to do. We do
not want to see many people and hope that the announcement of our
arrival in the papers will not lead to a number of unnecessary
or unwelcome visitors. About Eva I shall let you know as soon
as possible and we shall do our best to fix her up. In the mean-
time I hope that the arrangements in England are well under way.
We had a lot of children on board who very quickly got out of
control of their parents and made more noise than I ever expected
English children to do. - In the meantime I hope that Legintals
have moved in so that you have good company and help. I wonder
whether William is still there and who was with you all this time
and most of all whether you have had a quiet time or had to use
the old kitchen a lot. That is the worst of this distance that
such a lot of time must elapse until we hear from you. Don't for-
get to let me know how long this letter took, and when you write
tell me everything as much in detail as possible. We get a lot
of tomatoes and salad now, and that makes me think of Rosemount
each time. I hope that Manfred has been able to be with you at
least for a few days. Have you been in London in the meantime?
What about Heiner, Marta, Mama and all the others?

Kindest regards and best wishes
Lotte

Dear Hanna, we remember every moment our dear England
and follow all the news still with more eagerness than ever - as we
have not forgotten you. I have not yet all my lectures prepared
but I hope all will easily to be arranged on the way. The idea
that letters are taking still more time from South America is
very oppressive as we would like to hear every day from you and
to have your news as fresh as our eggs at Rosemount. Please tell
Eidemann that he may do after his own choice and go also farther
than I thought first, give him and everybody my best regards
Stefan Zweig

Dear Hannah, I wish to thank you for all the
trouble you will have with our house and other
affairs. Take nothing whatever serious. There are
in this moment thousands and hundred thousands
of men abroad and her matters have to wait, why
not just mine? Nothing is important than the
health of you all and I hope that with the com-
bination of Levin that all will go smoothly and
Manfred have his well deserved holiday. You
may imagine what good feeling it means to us
that we know all our affairs in the best hands and
I should be glad, if we could do something for
you all. You know that besides all my pessimism
which sees the things before they happen, there is a
good deal of optimism and I believe we will have
after some months of uncertainty again a fairly
quiet time; whatever happens after this war it will
easier to be bear than the continuous expectation of
evil and murderous surprise. Give my love to your
husband, your daughter, mother in law, sister and
brother and niece and to the whole house; we
will not forget you as far as we may be for
some time! Yours
Stefan

New York, 18.7.40

Dear Manfred,
I have to-day written to Hanna by
ordinary mail, but I hope that this letter
will reach you quicker. We have not had any
letters from you since we are here and I am
anxiously waiting for them. We are after all
not leaving for South America before the 9th Aug,
so you can write us c/o Viking Press and they would
forward by air any letters which arrive after
our departure.
I suppose you got the affidavit which
was sent to you last week for Eva through
Stephen Wise, whose wife is leading in the reception
committee. As soon as I know about the prospects of
Eva's coming I shall get in touch with them to
see where they propose to settle her. In the meantime
I am enquiring about boarding-schools and
among our friends. Anita Bahn from Frankfurt -
Hanna knows her - would take Eva for the be-
ginning, but perhaps I find a better solution
soon. My sister-in-law might also agree to take Eva
for a while but although she will be all-right
for taking her out or for holidays, I would not
recommend the atmosphere for more than a very
short time.
I hope that all of you keep well and
am impatiently looking forward to a letter.
There is so much we want to know about you, your
work, Rosemont, Heines and Marta and I hope you
have written long letters to New York.
Kindest regards, Lotte

pages.transcription:
Hotel Central (next adress will come by cable) 27. II 1940
Dear Hannah and Manfred, as you see we are preparing already our
next voyage and we have not yet quite decided, how to do it, by boat
or by plane. All is complicated as I have to visit the cities in the
North of Brazil, Bahia, Olinda, Pernambuco, the isle of Marajo —
it will be no pure pleasure to visit equatorial countries just in the
sammer time but we are „Kämmer quäler“ we know already what
a Brazilian summer has in store and support it quite well. The advantage
is that by this half the travel will cost nothing — the other half from
the frontier to the States is still expensive enough. Great difficulties means
the costume. On the plane we can have not much luggage, in North Brazil
it will have 40 degrees over zero and in Newyork 20 degrees under zero three
days later. But Lotte stands all this through much better than I thought and
we work every day, eating very little during the heat and sleeping much. All
the trouble of Brazilian summer-life could be averted with the expense of
a air conditioned room, an „anticearhaltring“? — then one could live even
in summer-time here and we love even now this wonderful city very much.
Now about you. Please have after a weeks rest in Bath, do spend freely
and do not worry, be sure that we shall look after Eva and give you more
news about her. You can thoroughly rely upon us. I hope Friedental got his
visa, the Argentine Consul makes it a speciality to make difficulties; he
had the telegrafic order for Landschoff and Friedental in the first days of
November and as he did not deliver it (to our astonishment) to Landschoff
who immediately applied, the Foreign Minister cabled a second time to de-
liver touristvisas to both, I cabled you the date of the second cable. Give
my love to Martha, to all friends, tell Flescher, that I had never a reply
on my letter to him and believe me yours sincerely and faithfully Stefan Zweig
Only a few words today as it is time to post the letter.
We are feeling hot but well and Stefan is glad of the good
chance to lose weight. Nevertheless, winter weather will be a
pleasant change, and I am looking forward to it and to seeing
Eva again.
Yours, Lotte.

28. July 1940
Dear Hannah, we are, as I wrote to Lotte in midst
of a heat wave and had today the hottest day since
four years 1940 but we do not feel much of it as our
rooms are fairly cool and all cafeterias ice cooled. So
do not pity us. We will have a kind of winter in Brazil
As to your daughter, Lotte has written to
you what happened. Stephen Wise has spontaneously offered
us to cable his affidavit and we were sure he has done
so. Unfortunately the same day appeared in all news-
papers the notice that the action has been stopped and
affidavits were superfluous. Now when suddenly the
American Government after three weeks offers slips
it seems that affidavits will have to be given again
and we do immediately all necessary steps. You know
me and Lotte enough to know that it was not our
fault but just this day when we were proud to have
settled all appears this notice and Stephen Wise
seems to have stopped his cable as superfluous
Yesterday we were invited at Reader's Digest
and I hope to write again something only not
like the last time without the expected result. I
join an interview with the New York Times so
that you may see, that we are busy here - we see
more people than we expected and time passes

quickly. We leave the 8th of August for Brazil, all
further arrangements will be made from there, where
we arrive the 21th of August.
You may imagine with how much eagerness
we follow all the news concerning England; the interest
and sympathy here is raising from day to day and
we hope that all possible help will be given to the
last country which fights for freedom. I suppose that
you have quiet days at Bath, sometimes we wish
to be there with you all, sometimes we wish to have

kindest regards from yours
Stefan Zweig

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, we have been so glad to have your letter. It
is such a misery now with correspondence — from South
America all replies came so late, from my former wife I
have no reply and have sent her at least five cables; we try to
get her a visa and can not let her know, what she on her part
has to do. So we have all our lot of excitement and you can
imagine what a sad surprise it was to know that the first affi-
davit for Eva has not been sent off — we had been so happy to
have arranged it the second day of our arrival in (as we be-
lieved) perfect way.
Now I have a favour to ask you: please dont worry about
the house and if you prefer to stay in London let it entirely
to the care of the gardener. It is so indifferent, all those
private things and belongings, compared with the great issue
and I would have a bad feeling to think that you are sepa-
rated from your husband only to be the keeper of the house.
Whatever you do you will never hear a reproach from me
I know you do the best, but I would no sacrifice of your
part; it would prefer to let fall it to pieces.
We leave this week for Rio, I have already invitations
from Uruguay and Venezuela, but I will stay if possible
in Rio for some time. The distances are enormous and
we have to wait how things develop. I am so sorry that
we could not wait till to Evas arrival. Lotte has done
her best to find her a good stay — unfortunately most of

pages.transcription:
our friends are absent or out of town, — in September all
will be returned — and so I had not so much opportunity
of choice. Your idea that Evas children should travel
with her seemed first very attractive, but you should not
bother about such things. Most important is that she
comes over without waiting to long; ~~all~~ all will be
arranged for her and she must not bring over much of
her clothes and matters, perhaps a little music for her study
but in any case not much. I hope in your and our all
interest that she will not have to stay long in America and
can soon be united with you again — I can understand
what it means to tear over an only child over the ocean.
But as thousands of mothers do the same and the whole
world is full of sufferings we have no right to complain.
We have been here some five days and I have worked
enough, but not enough to forget the time. You may imagine
how we follow all news in the newspapers — and how we will
be more away than before, thousands and thousands of miles!
One more thing, dear Hannah, please dispose freely of all
I have and do not be too economical for you all, it has no
sense and I am only pleased to know that I am not too
much in your moral debt for all what you do. From
Rio we can communicate only by night-letters as mail
would take months and our dispositions depend from the
circumstances. The most desirable would be, we could take
back Eva with us very soon. Sincerely to you all yours
Stefan Zweig

Wyndham Hotel				4.August 1940.

Dear Hanna,
I was so glad to get the first letter from you this
morning and to hear what is going on in "Rosemount" and in the
family. What a shame that Levintals did not come and apparently
let you down in not too nice a way! I hope that at least Orchard
found for you some nice people, for it is a terrible thought that
you should have to remain in Bath while the children are in London
only because there is no one else to look after it. I am glad that
you had Lizzie with you who is such a good friend to you, and I wish
I could be with you again. But we have to start travelling again on
Friday and have still a very busy time these last few days. Besides
packing and all the necessary formalities Stefan has started - at
first just for fun - to work on a film subject with a friend and now
they are working and dictating to me, and it takes most of our time
just now. Within the next few days I shall definitely decide where
Eva will stay - Rose is to bring me together with a family who are
very eager to take a child - and I shall then cable you the name
and address of Eva's future home and it will be best if you commu-
nicate directly with them. As I wrote you yesterday, my sister-in-
law offered to fetch her from the boat, and so will Rose if she is
back from her holiday - but I think it best if she goes directly
with the people where she will stay. But it is good to know that my
sister-in-law as well as Rose will later on visit her and see whether
she is well looked after and happy. My sister-in-law/s address is
Rose Wohl Stefanie Zweig, 18 West 70th Street, New York, and Roses 25 East
77th Street, New York, and I shall keep both exactly informed about
everything so that you can communicate with either of them if you
want to. - As to Eva's clothes, there is nothing specially American
you have to get for her. Just bear in mind that the summers are very
hot here, the winters very cold and that the houses are rather over-
heated than otherwise. Schools don't have uniforms. - As to bringing
Ursula over, I have little hope. The English reentry permit which
the Committee wrongly asked for Eva will, I am afraid, will be
essential for getting a visitor's visa for Ursula. And from what I
have heard so far from similar cases it is as good as impossible.
But I shall enquire again and let you know. -
We are sailing with the "Argentina"(American Republics
Line) on the 9th and should arrive in Rio on the 21st. If necessary
you could also cable us to the boat during the crossing. How long
we will stay there and where we go from then is not yet certain. Lat
on we hope to get permission to come back here, perhaps for a lect
tour. -
You did not say a word about Mama in your letter. I
suppose that means she is allright and still with Mathiasson.
We are happy to know that Orchard and Ingram are helpful and zeal friends
and that you also have good friends in London. Do you know by
chance whether Isaacs has taken over Korner's flat in Bath and
did you meet them? I liked them very much and I suppose you
would feel the same. Did you hear from Korner in the meantime?
Hoping that Eva will soon arrive safely and
that you are all keeping well,

7 sent this letter by clipper also				Lotte
pages.notes: Typoskript mit handschriftlichen Ergänzungen am linken Rand ('Rose Wohl') und am Ende ('7 sent this letter by clipper also').

Dear Hannah, a postscript. We have had
lunch with Mr. Salmon and I will tell
you frankly our impression - they are
nice people, she not too intelligent but
surely of good temper; they seem to have
a good income, perhaps they are "new
riches" who enjoy still her being wealthy
but not "wichtig" and very good-hearted.
I have the impression that Eva will be
quite happy there - of course, the fact of
being far
away from you will spoil a little her
happiness and if you are sincere to your-
self you would not wish, that it were
otherwise. My sister in law will also
be interested in her and Anita Calu
is also ready to expect her at the pier.
So do not worry too much: she will
see a new world and nobody knows
how such a connexion with America
can be valuable for her future.

pages.transcription:
By Clipper and by steamer

Dear Hanna and Manfred,
Finally I have settled Eva and I hope she
will be happy there, they are nice welltodo Americans, the man in
the smeltering business, kind-hearted, extremely fond of children,
jolly, their house in a very good neighbourhood in the suburbs of
Newyork - forty minutes by car - already countryside, near a lake.
I have not been out there myself as I spoke to Mr. Salmon only
yesterday and the wife is coming to Newyork to meet me - so I could
not insist on going out there especially as our time is now over-
crowded these last two days. But I am absolutely sure that there
is nothing to worry about the house and the surroundings. Rose
who brought me together with him told me that it is a very good
naighbourhood with excellent schoold and from what he told me it
is a very nice and large house and she will be looked after per-
fectly well. As they are definitely wealthy people there is nothing
to worry about from the financial point of view, he is eager to have
a child, to look after her, and what he would like best is to keep
her and marry her one day. He and his wife are college graduates,
she is, as he says "an artist", I believe she paints. He will see
that she continues her piano lessons, told me that there are plenty
of children in the neighbourhood, amongst them a thirteen year old
boy, a definite genius on the piano, and she will meet
nice children there. They are not too intellectual, but are having
a very good time, helping when they can, but enjoying life, and I
believe Eva will be in a pleasant and carefree atmosphere and feel
happy there. In any case Rose Wohl will go and visit her and let
me know how she is feeling there, and Rose also promised me to find
another home should this one not turn out as well as we expect. I
wish I could have stayed until Eva arrives, bring her to her new
home and see myself how she feels - but we have to leave, our time
is up and you know that we are expected to go to South America.
What you have to do now - if you have not
done so yet - is to cable Mr. Leon S. Salmon, 291 Beechmont Drive,
New Rochelle, New York, when Eva is arriving, so that he can fetch
her from the boat. He is very impatient to have her here, and I
hope you have not to wait too long for a boat and that she gets here
safely. Did you try the Palestine Orient Lloyd for a ticket? You know
we got ours there. -
I would also recommend that you cable also
Dr. Viola Wertheim Bernard (who was only the person to send the
affidavit as a special favour but who, I expect, will not take any
special interest in Eva) about Eva's arrival and where she is going
to live so that she is informed. I shall write her in any case and
tell her about it before I leave, but it is better that she knows
when Eva is coming and that she also informs the United States
Committee for European Children (215 Fourth Avenue) who want to
check up all the children whose affidavits went through their office
as Evas did.
I hope that Eva will not feel too lonely
arriving in a foreign country and being met by strange people, but
it cannot be helped. Rose might go down too to fetch her, but she
does not know her either.

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, for Eva all is now well prepared as you
have heard by our cable - they are wealthy people in a
large house in an elegant faubourg of Newyork and they
are really eager to have a good educated child. We see them
today for lunch. All was more difficult than we expected
as everybody is away from Newyork and this is also the major
difficulty for the affidavit for Heiner - I cannot ask one
from Heubal as he has given already too many and I do not
know if we can find anybody in these last two overcrowded
days. Till now I could not have any[?] definitive for my
former wife, I am trying now to get Mexican visas for
her whole family.
Thousand thanks that you have settled all about the
house in Bath, I hope you will have there sometimes a
good rest after the busy days in London.
We had here a hard time, as I have worked a good deal
merely small things, but we will have rest during the twelve
days on the ship. I have offers for lectures in Argentine
Uruguay, Chile, Venezuela, more than I will probably
do and you must not worry about us. Dont be too
economical and send us cables to Rio (from where we
send immediately our Hoteladress) - I do not
rely on airmail. In great love and hurry your
We arrive in Rio the 21. August                                Stefan

pages.transcription:
Rio 23. August 1940 Dear Hannah, we have been so glad
to get your letter from 8. August so quickly, the
others have not arrived yet except the first one.
Rio is as marvellous as ever, nothing in the
world to be compared with it. Unfortunately I am
afraid that Lotte will loose her modesty here since
she is always with ambassadors, ministers and
photographed in all newspapers. But we have plenty
of time for us, take three times a week Spanish
lessons as I have my lectures in the other countries
to deliver in Spanish - I do not know what to
accept, in Chile I am invited officially with the
obligatory visit to the President, in Uruguay I
have only two lectures and about three in Buenos
Ayres, provided I will do all this. Personally I
would like to stay here, we live here in a delightful
little hotel with all comfort in a nice apparte-
ment and very cheap - what a contrast with
Newyork, where one always has the feeling to be
a "Hochstapler" and where I had a good pretext
for not staying every day and to go with dirty
boots. On the ship it was delicious, 12 days of
perfect weather with swimming baths and a choice
of the most interesting and cultivated people. You
cannot imagine how refined and cultivated the
upper classes here are - a small élite but a
wonderful one: culture in houses, in manners
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig, violette Tinte. Sehr gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
and of a politeness, which even overshadows my
own. Lottes room is full of marvellous flowers, we
have autos for drives and in the same time they
are not insistant. The only thing which retreats me
to live here is the heat - we are arrived in full
winter but it is warmer than in Bath in July
and one shudders to think how it must be, when
spring commences (in October) and summer (in
December.)
The strangest thing is that I get quite indifferent
what happens with my books, that I do not
care to get no letters. I have got for my former
wife a visitors visit to America and possibly
one for Portugal but do not know if she will
leave without her children. All correspondence
with France is nearly impossible and I cannot
cable - by the way, cables from here are fright-
fully expensive, but do not hesitate to cable
us as often as you can. We shall stay here
in any case till to the first week of October
and possibly even longer but I am afraid
not much longer as we have to go then to
the other American countries which are some-
what cooler in summer (winter for you.) Here we
can follow all the events much better and
are much more confident; the sympathies in
South America for England are very great
and all is much more European - we hope that our best wishes
are with you all. Stefan
[Randnotiz links:] The United States, we hope you have a good time, a relatively
good one at Bath and you know that our best wishes
are with you all. Stefan

pages.transcription:
23.8.40
Dear Hanna and Manfred,
Yesterday we received your letter of the 8th
Aug. and on our arrival we found one of July 12th,
both air-mail, and that is all what we had from you
so far except that one clipper letter in London. It will
be best if in future you number your letters and I
confirm which one we receive. It is an event for me to
hear from you, and you can't write often and long enough.
For instance I do not quite know whether Marta was able
to stay with Manfred after all and if Rosa is still with him
also what you will do when Eva leaves, go back to
London? Please yourself entirely and don't think too much
of the house except as a place of rest and enjoyment
for you and Manfred. I know it will be hard for
you to be without Eva, but I hope that it will not
be for too long and that she will be happy with
Salmons. They are kind friendly people and I believe
not quite as rich as I first thought, just comfortably
off, earning well and as all Americans spending
freely. The only fear Mr Salmon expressed was
that they might get too attached to each other
and that it would be hard for Eva to leave
them again to go back home. But I assured
him that we prefer this by far and that I
would not worry about it now that she might
feel too happy in his family. I would hate
the thought that she is unhappy and just
longing to leave them. I asked Anita to
cable me when Eva arrives - I did not want
to confuse Salmon's by too many instructions -
but I would like you to
inform us also, by cable when you get the
news so that we know not only that Eva arrived
well but also that you know it were
informed about it.
About Heiner's affidavit. I cabled from here that
it would be sent from America soon by Jacob Landau.

[Randnotiz links:]
Also cable when Eva is sailing to New York
so that we can also
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf beidseitig beschriebenen Papierbögen. Die Randnotiz am linken Rand ist vertikal geschrieben.

pages.transcription:
Jacob Landau has travelled with us from New York.
He is director of the Jewish Telegraphic Agency in
New York and has cabled from here to his wife to
send the affidavit either herself or through his
office. It is a bit more complicated from here to
arrange it, but Mr. Landau feels confident that
the affidavit can be sent in his absence. He is a
very decent man and will certainly see to it - al-
though by correspondence only - that the matter is
not neglected. I certainly have learned from
the affair with Eva's affidavit. Let us hope that
it helps Heiner to get over, and if Alice is willing
to work in a household she will easily
find work, and then she can slowly build
up a business for herself.
As to us: we had a beautiful crossing
with very nice South-Americans and are being
spoilt here. I must admit that in spite of
all the events and in spite of the fact
that I always feel a little homesick for
you, the former Bath-family and Bath itself,
we really enjoy it here. Rio is just as
beautiful as Stefan promised, the people just
as nice as he said and the winter not hard,
one feels just right in a light summer dress
and I need not have brought my winter things
for this Brazilian winter.
We were glad to get your cable on the
ship and to learn that Manfred spent the weekend
of Eva's birthday with you. I wish we could have
been with you. I hope you are all well. Please give
Mama my love and tell her about my letter, I shall
write her soon and perhaps enclose a few photos
made on our arrival.
Kindest regards to all, especially to
Lizzie who seems to have developed into our caretaker.
Letter No. 2 from Rio. Lotte

letter 4 from Rio

Hotel PAYSANDÚ
6.9.40

Dear Hanna, dear Manfred,
I have just written a long letter to Mama and do not
feel energetic enough to write you as well especially as I wrote you at
length a few days ago. Just one little thing about Mama: She wrote
me that she was going to change over to the small single room and
I asked her in my letter to keep hers. You have plein pouvoir to
settle the one-pound-difference from our account, and more, if
necessary. - I hope you are still all well and as cheerful as
your last letter from Bath indicated. I am waiting to hear
about Eva. Has Manfred to go ~~out~~ much work and must he go out
at all times? - We are well and happy here and have equipped ourselves
for the summer which we will have here and in the other countries
until December. We continue to work in the mornings, go out in the
afternoon, learn Spanish, meet quite a lot of people, I am con-
centrating hard on names and faces and feel very proud that I
recognise most people, even in other surroundings. I am reading the
war reports every day and learn a lot of Portuguese thereb. Although
these reports are very long I do not think they say any more - or
perhaps not even as much - as you read in the English papers. -
From common acquaintances we met Mryn's. They feel quite well
here but he has not yet found anything. - We will be here until
middle of October and then inform you by cable. But the postal
address will remain Editora Guanabara.
Kindest regards for everyone, love and kisses for you,
Lotte

Until middle of October
HOTEL PAYSANDÚ, Rio

who will forward letters

Rio, 10.9.40

Dear Manfred and Hanna,
Thanks for your cable that Eva has
sailed. I hope she has a very good journey and will feel happy in
her new surroundings. I asked Salmon's to cable me her arrival and
I hope you will do so as well. We are of course very anxious to
have news from you, and please write often. I was surprised that
our letters had not yet arrived because we wrote at least once a week
from here. We only write by air from here, and I expect you get a few letters
at once. We address them to your London address. I hope that you are all well
when this letter arrives. And if you think it better that Mama leaves
tell her not to worry about the cost and I hope she will get permission
to leave and go wherever she wants as I do not think that she may go to
Bath. - We are perfectly well in these wonderful surroundings
and shall be sorry to leave in the middle of October. But Rio is getting
very hot in November, and so Stefan will give a few lectures in
Uruguay Argentine and Chile. There is a possibility that we travel
from Buenos Aires to Chile through the Straits of Magellan, but that is yet
uncertain. We expect to be in Chile in December and in January in
New York. - we got our visas, visitor visa for lectures, today. - Here
in Brazil Stefan will go to Sao Paulo for a day for a lecture, and then
we are invited by the Governor of Minas Geraes to see his Province where
there are interesting old towns like Ouro Preto and Mariana, a gold mine
etc. As we will go by air we will be away from Rio not more than
2 or 3 days. 
Kindest regards and love,
Lotte
We would be perfectly happy here would it not be for you. Lotte be-
hares here like a great lady and besides machines, is photographed
and to be seen in all the newspapers in all her beauty. In the
evening we feel always completely confused by speaking all[?] in
quick turns English, French, Spanish, German, Yiddish, Portuguese;
you will see in our letters, that we are not more able to write
correctly any language. Next week I have a full program and

pages.transcription:
№ 6 or 7 from Rio

Rio
Sunday, 15.9.40

Dear Hanna and Manfred
Just now I got a telegram that Meiner's affidavit
has been cabled. I do not yet know any details besides this
and shall phone Mr. Landan to Sao Paulo to-night in
order to hear more and then I shall send you a cable.
Within the next few days I also hope to get a cable in-
forming me of Eva's arrival in USA. I believe I confirmed
already your letter of Aug 26th. I am glad that you still enjoy
Bath and I hope you will have a relatively calm time and
if possible with Manfred. What about Mama? Did you try to
get permission that she leaves London? I am afraid she will
not be allowed to go to Bath, but perhaps she can go with
some friends. Yes, Manfred is right, we follow with great
concern all the newspaper reports and I nearly wish some-
times that I could be with you in order not to have to
wait so long for news. On the other hand, I cannot deny
that we enjoy our stay here enormously. We have today
changed over to other rooms looking out on the bay, and
this little detail will make it more difficult for us
to leave Rio. Up to now it is not yet very hot, and the
weather is just perfect for strolling around and making
excursions. Friday Stefan has a lecture in Sao Paulo and
as I was invited as well I shall accompany him although
I do not expect too much from this town except a visit to
the snake farm where they make serum against snake bites.
I hope to have another letter from you within
the next few days and wish that it contains good news.
All the best wishes to all of you,
Lotte

Rückseite des Dokuments, leer.

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, it is not at all easy for us to write
to you. We read in the newspapers about the furious attacks on England
(happily also that they are rebated) and we feel ashamed to have here
such a perfect life. To look out of our windows is simply a dream, the
temperature is superb - a winter which is more June than May - the
people treat us in every possible way, we live quietly, deeply and the
most interesting life - really happy would it not be for you and all the
friends and the great misery of mankind. I will do everything to prolong
our stay here as Lotte will absolutely not leave, but I have to fulfil my
duties. I have a lecture in San Paolo this week, very well paid, 250
dollars and hotel and plane for us both, this covers alone one whole
month and I have no material worries as the lectures in Uruguay,
Argentine, Chile are equally well paid and we are invited in Uruguay
and Chile as guests of the Government, which will pay railway and
hotels. Next week we are going to the old towns in the interior of Brazil
as guest of the Province, poor Lotte will be photographed abundantly and
here you could see her in all the cinemas. Finally we go back to New York
we have already our visas and shall see (and let us hope so) and
fetch Eva. You may be both sure that we will look after her and
bring her back grown-up and perhaps with a Yankee-accent.
It is terrible for me to remember all the friends there over. I hope
that Robert Neumann and Korner[?] could leave, we have done all
for an American visa during my stay. Friedental I cannot help
from here except if he would like to go to Brazil or to Cuba - in
January I will try all possible. My former wife has her visas to
America and I believe also to Mexico, she is thanks to the help of
Ferro, who has been very kind to me, in Lisbon. But all the others. You
will understand how ashamed we feel here and I should be glad
to know that you can enjoy Bath in theses days of wrath. Please
be generous with money, nobody knows what the next years will
bring and I should be so glad to be of any help to you, to your
family and our friends. Yours
Stefan Zweig

we cable yesterday

L. L. war eben bei Wooster wegen näherer Central-
heizung. Der Mann ist unglaublich anständig, riet mir ab
neuen Ofen zu kaufen, behauptet, es genüge ~~außerhalb des sink~~ {eingefügt: unterhalb des sink}
guten Boiler zu transferieren. Für die Küche und Bad
empfiehlt er die Wasserheizung (Gas) zu mieten, weil dann
die Leute verlässlicher alle Reparaturen machen. All das
scheint mir die ideale Lösung — unten Centralheizung, in
den Schlafzimmern Gas oder Elektrik, da man sie unter Tag
doch kaum benützt und ist auch nachts es wohl gerne so
warm in den Zimmern habe. Damit ist das hier uns herlaafen
zu alten Küche erledigt: ein Kohlenofen wird im Winter
täglich geheizt, teils Monate, die übrige Zeit Gas und Elektrik.
Er sagte mir zu in verzehn Tagen, sobald er die
Stelle umplant habe, so viele Arbeiter zu herfahren zu haben
als er wolle. Er lasse uns bekommen nicht in Stich.
Wenn es Dir keine Reihe macht bringe den Baker
mit, er kann aber ebenso in der kleinen Kammer bleiben und
die nimmt allenfalls Dinge, die Dir wichtiger sind.
Herzenst
Die harder kommt ausserhalb

much practical about house-furnishing and house-keeping.
I believe it will {eingefügt: become} now, as we cut the old kitchen entirely
out (reserving her to become a Wasch- und Bügelraum)
a snug little house with all possibilities of later expansion
and this seems to me the ideal solution in those enigmatical
times. I hope Manfred will not go immediately go to France
- it is very easy {eingefügt: to get} in their such an obligation but
very difficult to get out again. „Gehe nie zu einem
Ferscht wenn du nicht gerufen werst“ [?] — His
law I learnt in my schooldays and my later
experiences have proved the thruth of this profound

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, as Lotte is lazy and writes only short
letters it is to the Hausbuch[?] to write all what happened. We
like the city and the people enormously and we are delighted
how much sympathy in all the important quaters exists for
England, how much pity for France; the newspapers are in contrast
with the Northamericans absolutely partial for England and express
openly the hope that Hitlers attacks will fail. English ships come
from time to time but one does better to write by air over
Newyork, it takes sometimes only 10 days. My plans are not
quite definite, I have a lecture, well paid, in San Pablo and
here I will there for speak for some charitable purpose, then
Uruguay 2 lectures and Buenos Aires and Chile; our expenses will
largely be covered and I have time to write meanwhile. I ad-
mire Rio every day more, it is the most colourful, the most
fascinating town I know, full of surprises and new beauties; it
develops with a rapidity what seems unbelievable - we went
to day in the tram just an hour (for two American cents) and
have not seen half of the city. Today we had two receptions
Lotte had not less then four ministers for conversation (and
with the former ambanador Cortin five) first at the reception
for the Uruguay minister, where she sat at the side of the foreign
minister then in a party given in her honour (or ours) at the
minister of communications - one charming house and with lots of
gardens with views one only can dream. Yesterday we had long
nightly auto drives along the ocean and over the mountains, to
morrow we have the minister of Cuba for tea and meanwhile she
fits and talks, - often too much because I want to explore
this town and there are so many parts we have not yet inspected.
I would like to live now there except here would it not be for
the heat which hinders my work as I was able to see in Newyork
- but they are already constructing air conditioned houses here

letter Nr.7. from Rio
22.9.1940.

Dear Hanna and Manfred,
I have not had a letter from you last week, ~~but~~ and
I have not received the cable of Eva's arrival either, but I hope that both
will arrive to-morrow, and that you will be able to inform me that you have
a quiet time in Bath and that Manfred is not too worn out. I write a letter
to Mama to-day which I address to Woodstock Road as I hope that she has
been able to leave London, and if not for Bath, at least for the country
with a friend. - We have, as in the last weeks always, only to report a
lot of social life, invitations, receptions, presents of flowers and books,
and the only drawback - besides the fact that these masses of people and
their kindness is somewhat confusing and also tiring - is that Stefan does
hardly find any time for his work. The free time he has had during the
last week has mostly been taken by the preparation of his lectures, trans-
lations into English, French and ~~xxxxxxx~~ Spanish, revisions, retranslations
and the Spanish lessons. But at least Stefan understands now Spanish and
Portuguese quite well and talks Spanish, if necessary, and I am also able,
although with some difficulty, to follow a conversation in Spanish as well
as in Portuguese, and I manage to make myself understood by the porters in
the hotel of whom only one speaks English and the others no foreign language
at all. - We have just returned from Sao Paulo where Stefan gave a
lecture, the first in Brazil. We have flown there Friday in 1 1/2 hours,
attended a luncheon in our honour with all the obligatory flowers, photo-
graphers and speeches, were taken for a sight-seeing tour in the town and
found very little to see, and in the evening after the lecture went to
another reception where we stayed until after midnight. The next morning
Stefan went to see the building of the newspaper who had invited him for
the lecture, and I was visited by Roselotte and Yorg who send their kindest
regards and say that they had thought of inviting Eva for the duration and
are willing to take her even now should you so desire. At two we were
again taken to the airport, and after a half hour of polite conversation
with all the people who had come to see us off, flew back to Rio, and to-
day we are firmly determined not to accept any visitors and invitations and
to have a very quiet day. Tuesday morning we are flying to Minas Geraes to
visit some old and interesting towns in that province, Ouro Preto, Mariana
etc. and we intend to be back on Thursday. We shall probably also go to
Bahia for a few days, and we have invitations to go to a fazenda in the
interior, for a lecture in Santos, and to travel on the rio San Francisco.
Whether we shall be able to do all that, is still uncertain. Stefan is not
yet quite decided whether he shall really go to Chile and whether we shall
not instead remain in Brazil a little longer and then return to USA directly
from here or perhaps from Buenos Aires. In any case the postal address
will remain c/o Editora Guanabara, and the telegraphic address we ~~will~~ will
cable you always. Kindest regards to you all, keep well and write fre-
quently. I intended to write to Lizzy for a long time, but and I shall do
so soon. I hope that she is still with you in Bath, and I would not be
surprised to hear that you have some more friends out there now. I hope
you have received the affidavit for Heiner. I was only informed that it
had been cabled, without any details, and although I asked for more detailed
information I have not yet received it. We had a cable from Eisemann that
he is back home. Kindest regards from Lotte, we should like to hear from here.
Best love and kisses, Lotte

All is perfect here, we see the best and nicest people and would love only to have a day
without our photos in the newspapers and the stories where we have been and what we have done.
Anyhow I will see as much of this fascinatoy country as possible and it will give together
with my former notes a nice little book. Lotte has become very talkative in society and
is in great love with Rio like myself - why has this country only five month in the
year with temperate climate? I have had here Kenneth Tynan from the Ministry and will
have Rio-Rio, give a little lecture also for the English circle in English - developing in a bird
of lecturer in form of five languages. If only we were not so anxious about you we would
* Bahia is as far from here like Madrid from Roscan - we we really need travellers.
pages.notes: Typoskript mit handschriftlichen Ergänzungen am Rand und am Ende des Dokuments.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer.

pages.transcription:
2)
I am glad to know you settled again in a comfortable warm flat
and that you can even stay there at night, and I can hope for
nothing better than that you will be able to remain there until
the end of the war. It is still a strange thought to me when I
think of you in London to place you to Regency Lodge and no more
in Woodstock Road and I found lots of memories to write me to
the old house. I also thought of you at Christmas time, how different
it was for all of us this year. But the main thing is that you spent
a good time here and that Manfred had a real rest, I am sure he
needed it as well as you, Hanna after the removal. - Your friend Paul
suddenly appeared last week, he arrived on a cargo liner with wife,
child, Lubitza and a few cases of books and manuscripts, and
Stefan became jealous, and we admired them because they immediately
took a furnished flat while we are living in one hotel room. He came
as chairman of the United Correspondents and seems to be getting on well
because he did not phone the whole week. When we met him, they were
still a little bewildered and hardly told any stories.
I am afraid I must stop. I see Stefan has written a lot
and otherwise the letter gets too heavy. Kindest regards and kisses,
write often! Lotte
