pages.transcription:
Hotel Paysandú, Rio 29. Sept. 1940
letter 8 from Rio
Dear Manfred and Hannah, you write that you want long letters — alas, it
is the only thing we can do for you. I am ashamed to say that all is perfect
here, the climat delicious (now in winter time) the people wonderful and all sym-
pathies on the side of England. We just came back from the interior, where we
were invited by the Governor of the province Minas Geraes; we were taken to the
capital in an a plane, had an autocar with a charming secretary of the ministry
all the time at our disposition and were brought back in two days auto-travelling
through the country. By that we have seen a lot and the real life of Brasil. Next
week we will go somewhere in the mountains to have a rest {before we leave} — we are not tired,
not in the least, but I want to do some {afterwards} here we are bombarded with
invitations, interviews and I am looking forward for a few days without speaking
in five languages to two hundred people and not to have our picture in the paper.
If it would be for Lotte, we would not leave at all Brasil, she is very changed
and is restoring me every moment in her exalted way with exclamations. Is it
not marvellous and so on and ? have married her just because she has been formerly
so discret, but I have to do my duty and we will leave about the 22 October.
I have two lectures in Montevideo and will give two at Buenos-Aires and two
in the universities of Cordoba and Rosario. They had made me a programme of
six lectures in Buenos Aires, but I have enough. The lectures are well paid and
we can make easily our living from it, so I do not want to make a profession
out of it. Later on I should go to Chile and Venezuela and Cuba, I have from
everywhere urgent offers, I think however I will not accept them and you will
understand it if you look on the map, what enormous distances that means.
And all the receptions in all these little countries, the noisy publicity are against
my conception of life. It is good to know, that I could make my living for
months and months going around as a lecturer but we prefere a more quiet way
and it is impossible to write in midst of such travelling, thanks God, I am not
gready neither for money nor for honours. By the way, please dispose of my
accounts for you and your family as it were yours and I would be grateful
if you would sent to friends like Friedental or Pleinher something to relieve
her situation, I feel somewhat guilty that I have here all honours and a decent
living through my work while you are disturbed in your profession and have gracious
days and nights. Please believe me that I do not care at all for the house and the
property; we are all reduced to the minimum of what men can ask from life —
life itself and this is already much in these days. And now to Eva. I am sure she
My former wife could come to Lisbon and is already on the way overseas, and how many are
still in France. Even here we get letters and telegrams from all sides.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Der Text am linken Rand ist vertikal geschrieben. Die Tinte ist violett.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer.

pages.transcription:
will feel all right at Salmons and please dont forget that we shall be in three
months ourselves at Newyork and I hope you know that we are reliable and that
Eva will have a second mother and a good uncle. About her musiclessons I wrote to
her, You may imagine how gladly surprised I was to hear from her progress. So you may
be without any worries about her and about us. Please send us often cables, it has
not sense to be on your side parsimonious and perhaps you can send them even
with paid answer so that you may be sure that we are always able to give you notice
about our whereabouts. Dear Hannah and Manfred, I know it is a hard moral task for
you not to envy us who can continue our work quietly and in a beautiful surround-
ing but I feel that your good wishes are with us as ours are always with you. Stefan
postal address from now on, even when we have left Brasil:
Dear Hanna and Manfred, c/o editora GUANABARA, 132 Rua Ouvidor, Rio de Janeiro
Today we got your and Mama's letter of the 12th Sept.
after two weeks without news except the cable about Eva's arrival. Please do
not forget that I wait just as impatiently for your letters as you for ours and
write regularly and as often as possible, if only a few lines. If I cannot be
with you, I want at least to know everything about you and our friends. I hope
you had a few days rest in Bath. We had a letter from Ingram yesterday and
write him and Mr. Orchard by airmail today. I am glad that you can rely upon
their advise and help if necessary. Has Lorle been alone with Ursel in the house
all the time, except for Griffith? I was sorry to hear that Mr. Miller is ill,
I hope he will recover again, he belongs to my memory of the house just as much
as you and the children and Marta. Is Alice still in Baker Street? I hope the
affidavit for Heiner has arrived by now. Mr. Landau assured me that it had been
cabbed but he had himself no detailed news about it, as he was travelling about
and got no letters himself but only cables. - I cannot tell you how glad I
was that you cabled me Eva's arrival. I got your cable Sunday afternoon and I
read the news about the ship disaster in the Atlantic about an hour before
Salmon's cable arrived. What a shock it must have been for you and what a
relief that she was not only on the other ship but already safely arrived. I
have not yet a letter from her, but I suppose it is on the way. I wrote her
last week and am writing her again today so that she does not feel all alone,
even though I feel sure that she is already on the best of terms with Mr. and
Mrs. Salmon. She will just have arrived in time for the new term in school and
Mr. Salmon assured me that there were excellent public schools in New Rochelle,
and that they knew plenty of children in the neighbourhood. My sister-in-law
was already in touch with Mrs. Salmon before Eva's arrival and will certainly
have visited her by now, and I suppose Rose will go to see her too, so that I
will have reports from them soon. - I hope that you are all in good health and
that you are not too much exhausted by the lack of sleep and the continous
excitements. I am glad that you have a good shelter at last and that you are
even able to sleep there. Has Manfred to go out a lot or has his practice gone
down with the latest events? I could also imagine that he has a lot more to do
and I only hope that he has not to go out during an attack. We think of you more
often than you imagine and the people here too are very sympathetic to the cause
of England. - From ourselves I can only repeat that we have a much too good
time, that everybody is extremely nice and that the only drawback is that they
are even too nice. We have so many invitations and the newspapers are so in-
terested in what Stefan does that we consider going to a small place in the
mountains nearby at the end of this week so that Stefan can work quietly at
least for a few days and that our brains can have a rest from the continual
change of faces before us and of the change of languages in the conversation.
Last week we have been in the province of Minas, as Stefan wrote, and it was
very interesting to travel through the country.
Kindest regards to you all, Lotte

pages.transcription:
Therezopolis, 6.10.40
Dear Hanna and Manfred,
I write rather in a hurry for
we have just arrived here for a weeks' rest, and Stefan's
editor and his wife who brought us here in their car,
are still with us and waiting to take us round and
show us the town or village, whatever it is. I hope that
you are all well, that Manfred has not too much work
and was able to take a few days rest in Bath with
you, Hanna. How I wish we could be there together, soon.
From Eva I only had a cable announcing her arrival,
and a letter from Stefan's brother that Salmon's post-
poned their visit to New Rochell twice because Eva was
invited. I suppose that Eva has a very good time,
and probably they sent her letter to my by ordinary
mail so that it will arrive here only in about a fortnight
just before we leave for Argentine.
Kindest regards and kisses,
Lotte.
Dear H. a. M. we are looking every days through all newspapers
for good news and follow all the events - we hope the best for you. We regret
very much to leave Brazil for here true the 26. October - we has here an ex-
cellent time. We have seen the most wonderful houses, my publisher brings us
everywhere we like in his car, our friend the Viscount Arcuri de arrange all
social thing for us in a splendid way, the Ambassador of Cuba sends me
nearly every week a box of Havannahs and on every corner are coffeehouses.
We live very dearly here and see a lot - all would be perfect if how
the anxious thoughts about you. I suppose we will leave our Chile and
Venezuela, I am not willing to travel too much as I have no heart to
work and one has to do his work even in these times. I hear that
Robert Hermann is back again, I wish I knew his adress as I would
like to let him know that we do not forget him. Love Stefan

pages.transcription:
c/o Editora Guanabara
132 rua Ouvidor, Rio de Janeiro.

Teresopolis, 10.10.40

Dear Hanna and Manfred,
I was very happy to get your letter of the 24th Sept. to-day and to
hear that up to that date you were all well and bearing the strain of war-life
without too much difficulty. Of course we are always anxious about you when we
read the news of air-attacks in the paper and therefore we asked you to cable, if
at all possible once a week. It was not quite clear from your letter, Hanna, if
Manfred was still with you in Bath - I hope he was able to stay a few days and
have a good rest. I would like to know about his work and whether he as a
doctor has to go out also during an air-raid or whether perhaps he is now also
employed in a hospital. I hope that Mama has by now been able to leave
London. I can understand the difficulties and that in a way she prefers to
stay but on the other hand there is no point in her staying where she is
if she has a possibility to go to a quieter place. I cannot tell you how happy
we are to know Eva safe and settled. We had the first letter from her to-day,
saying that she is very happy there, that school is very nice and that Salmon's
have a huge Alsation dog. Mr. Salmon added a note how happy he is to have her
and that they are already very great friends. Eva also writes that my sister-
and brother-in-law have been there. The shock of reading in the paper the
news of the disasters, was as great for us as it was for you, and I can under-
stand how you feel about it. That thought haunted us for days. Fortunately
your cable had arrived the night before, because Salmon's cable only arrived
hours after we had read the news in the paper. Well, at least she is safely
at Salmon's, apparently quite happy about everything. I am sure my
sister-in-law has written me about her visit, but apparently a few
letters, mostly air-mail which were forwarded to us from Rio, have been
lost. That is the great drawback of this place where we are staying.
Everything else is perfect here, the landscape beautiful, we are right in the
mountains, 3000 feet high and yet there is something tropical about it, orangetrees,
banana trees, bamboo, we have lovely rooms with a big terrace where we work,
a swimming pool, dogs, food cooked by Czechs - but the mail from Rio takes several
days and sometimes does not arrive at all. Now we have found out that there
exists a tradesman who comes up from Rio every day - it is 3 hours by car-
and that's why your letter was not lost. And this gives Stefan courage to consider
coming here again for a fortnight after he has done his duty and went
to Argentine and Uruguay for the lectures. According to our present plans
we fly to Buenos Aires on the 26th (six hours), stay there a fortnight to 3 weeks,
go for a few days to Montevideo, then come back up here to Teresopolis
for a fortnight's rest which will be necessary after a few weeks continuous
receptions, lectures and whole-day politeness in various languages. This place
where we are now staying, is ideal for working and rest, and as the lighting
system is still a little medieval - the light depends on the water supply and
it had not rained for a few months and so it is rather sickly and weak -
we go to bed very early and get up at 7, so that the morning is enormous.
by long and leaves us a lot of time for work and walk and a swim if
we feel like it. Although it is only spring now, it is already very warm and
while you will be glad with some kind of heating (by the way can you heat the
shelter and which room do you use in Bath for it?) we will have a rising
temperature until we get to New York. Fortunately we found out in the New York
heat wave that we both support it well, and up here in Teresopolis the night
are always cool. So this problem does not worry us, even if we should have
to stay in South America longer than we intent to now.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig, violette Tinte auf rosa Papier. Sehr gut lesbar.
Rückseite der ersten Seite, durchscheinender Text des Briefes von der Vorderseite.

pages.transcription:
You do not write, Hanna, how long you are staying in Bath. In any case I am glad that
you have filled the house with friends and that it helps a few people to
get some rest, and it will be good company for you and for the children.
Please thank Ursula and Lotte for her letter. Is she going to school as usual? I am sorry
to hear that Alice lives in such a menaced district and more sorry that
apparently again something is wrong with Heiner's affidavit which should
have arrived long ago. I hope you will cable as soon as this is settled
for him, although it would be a more anxious thought than ever to have him
them on the ocean. - Do continue to write often and in detail. There is always a
possibility of a letter getting lost, especially in South America, and I am always
impatiently waiting for the weekly letter. I suppose Eva will write you
regularly and in any case you know that we are in touch with her, that
Mr. Salmon is apparently delighted with her and that as long as we are
not in USA, my sister-in-law and Rose will visit her from time to
time. Give my kindest regards to all the inhabitants of Rosemount and
Woodstock Road, I am glad that they still remember us and I wish nothing
better than to refresh this memory in person very soon together with my
lawful wedded husband. 
Best wishes and kisses to you both,
Lotte

Dear H & M. I cannot tell you how happy I am that the house in Bath is of such a good use and that
we can be helpful to our friends. You will understand how we feel all the difference of fate,
that I by my duty and work have to be in the most fascinating surroundings while you live under
the menace of our common enemy. I have seldom in my life seen a finer place, quiet, the house
tasteful, the house people thinking the whole day what to do for us our cooling all because dishes
we have not had since years. And peculiar charm in midst the tropical nature: the negros working in
the same oven like in the slavery-days only happy and always smiling, fat pigs, horses, a really
dream-hacienda. And what have we seen in Rio: the most perfect houses with gardens covering
a whole mountain and on the other hand the popular life. Now I have to pay for all that with
a gunfire of lectures, two in Rio next week (in French) three then in Buenos Aires (in Spanish)
and one in English/ two in Rosario and Cordoba, two in Montevideo; they pay very good and all
our expenses are largely paid. We live here in our normal way with everything we want, avoi-
ding carefully the luxury-hotels and you can not imagine the kindness of the people. Instead
to go to Chile and Venezuela we will return here to Brazil, I have still to go to Bahia, the
most picturesque place and probably we will do it in a small steamer to see all the little
old towns on the coast - a glance on the street with all the coloured people in all humble
uniforms is an inexhaustible delight! Pardon my English. By reading Portuguese, speaking French
and Spanish I have lost the orthography and do often not know what language I use or misuse.
I have not forgotten the house but since I know that it is such a good shelter for friends (kindest
regards to all) I feel much less remorse; on the contrary! Sometime I wish I could change with
you for a week not to have all this lucky time for us alone and to share your harder life.
I see there is no justice in the world. Countabout the new year we hope to be with Eva
and you understand that we cannot give approximate [?] our plans
invitations, obligations, ship departures and not in the least from the development of the

Rio, 16.10.40

Dear Hanna and Manfred,
There is not much to write to-day. We had a very
pleasant and extremely quiet week in the mountains where
Stefan got all his favourite dishes, where he could work
quietly and where we had nice people to talk if we wanted
to. Now we try to accustom our ears again to the noise of
Rio and think of the noise you must endure. We expect to
have a very lively week before going to Buenos Aires and will
probably have a rather hectic time there. In the middle of
November we intend to be in Montevideo and by the end
of December in New York where Eva is the only attraction.
We hope that you all have not too bad a time
and could good wishes help, England would have won already.
Stefan is trying to get a visa for his friend Friedenthal here and
maybe even a modest job, but he does not know how to
communicate with him, and then vises have become almost as
difficult here as in America, or even more so as there are no
rules but only silent restrictions.

Kindest regards to all, kisses to you both,
Lotte

pages.transcription:
letter Nr 8 from Rio.
Rio, 19th October 1940

Dearest mother,
I got to-day your letter of Oct 1st, addressed to
New York, and I hope that you live now in a quieter place. As
I wrote you already, do not economise now, I shall be glad if
at least our money can be of some use now and if I know you at
least as comfortable as it can be. I often try to imagine what
life must be in a town so acutely at war as London, but my
imagination fails me and I can only admire and pity those who
continue to work and live under such a strain. When we meet
people who have lived in England and who have still commu-
nication with it, we invariably sit together and exchange
bits of information and feel somehow homesick although we know
of course how lucky we are not to live through the war night
and day. I expected already before your letter arrived that you
might leave London, and my last letters to you I addressed
to Manfred. I am afraid that he, as a doctor cannot help
going out under any conditions, and I suppose that he told
Hanna to remain in Bath. At any rate they will be glad to
know you are safe, and I believe quite happy in her new surroundings.
I suppose we will see her at the end of December. - I repeat
our next plans: 26th by plane to Buenos Aires (in 6 hours), about a
fortnight in Argentine where Stefan has about half a dozen
lectures, also a little in the country universities, then a few
days Uruguay with one or 2 lectures in Montevideo, and then
a few weeks more in Brazil, presumably in Terezópolis where
it does not get so hot. Now it is only spring and the temperature
very agreeable, and anyhow, as we lived through a heat wave
in New York and stood it quite well, we are not afraid of
heat. - We regret to leave Brazil, and it is only out of a
sense of duty, to fulfil his promise, that Stefan decided to
give all his lectures in Argentine and Uruguay. We have
made a few real friends among the hundreds of people we
met, and that gives one a little a feeling of belonging to a place.
pages.notes: Briefkopf der Editora Guanabara. Handschriftlicher Text in violetter Tinte.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, leer.

pages.transcription:
2)
We still enjoy the beauty of Rio, and although lately we
did not find much time for excursions, every walk or
drive in the tram - there are buses as well, but we prefer
the old-fashioned, open trams - is a pleasure as regards natural
beauty and local colour. Stefan is trying hard to work re-
gularity, but in Rio itself it is very difficult with all the
engagement, invitations and now the practical travel arrangements.
Besides this people have a lot of time here, and there is still
the good old habit that the men drop in for a little chat
in the afternoon, and three times a week Stefan had his
Spanish lessons as he will speak in Spanish in some of the
places in Argentine and Uruguay. I have given up attending
his lessons. It is impossible for me to keep Spanish and
Portuguese apart as I hear and read both languages at the
same time, and I have made up a language of my own which
combines both and somehow is understood. With all our
invitations we have not been in a concert, theatre or film
the whole time except once at a first night of a Portuguese
play. Last night I heard the radio also for the first time
since we are here, and it was the English news service from
the BBC, and a strange feeling to hear it so far away. As we
were all people who had lived in England a long time, we
became quite sentimental about this fact. - I hope that you
have in the meantime got the photos which I sent a long
time ago. Fortunately the daily photographs have stopped and
the papers only report, as they do with every person who is
a little known to the public, what we do and what we are
supposed to do. On the whole we have had a quieter time
lately and met mostly people we knew at the various
places we went to, and as a special treat our friends invite
only a few other people with us instead of twenty unknown
persons which keep one occupied the whole evening by the effort
to remember with whom one was talking. Altogether we have
pages.notes: Zweite Seite des Briefes, handschriftlich.
Rückseite des zweiten Blattes, leer.

pages.transcription:
3
had a time here which would have been absolutely
perfect if it were not for the thought of all the people
in Europe which is continually in our mind. Stefan
could not have had a nicer reception here, and if the
too great publicity was sometimes a nuisance, it was in
itself well-meant. In any case we both love Brazil very
much, and should we be forced to choose, we would pre-
fer it greatly to USA. But I hope this choice will not
be necessary and that everything comes to a good end
quicker than we all dare to hope now.
Kindest regards and kisses
Lotte.

Best wishes from Stefan

Kindest regards to Manfred and Hanna I
await their next letter before I write to them.

132 RUA OUVIDOR, Rio

Rio, 23. X. 40

Dear Hanna and Manfred
I just got your letters from Bath (30.9. and 2.10.)
and I write immediately although we are again feeling like in a
madhouse - leaving Saturday for Buenos Aires, to-day Stefan's con-
ference in French "Vienne d'hier", since two hours a phone call from
Buenos Aires announced without name and not yet come through,
urgently some books to sign for people who are leaving Rio to-day,
to-morrow a Jewish charity affair where Stefan has to speak an intro-
duction, a men's luncheon to-morrow and the last rehearsal of the Spanish
lecture on Friday. In between Stefan dictates a lecture in English,
that is to say I shall translate it and he will revise it, another lecture
for the refugees in Buenos Aires and he revises his other lectures in
French which he might have to give, and sometime I shall have to pack
- and pack carefully because we fly and I have to select what to take.
I sign the form of the Westm. Bk and Stefan will decide soon about the
other authorisation and send it, I suppose, when we will again have
a free moment. - It gave me quite a shock that you had to transfer
part of your furniture, but please always write about everything, I
fear nothing more than to have to think that you hide anything
that has happened. About the cables: We prefer that you send them
every week or fortnight, letters are so irregular, sometimes a fortnight
nothing and then English air-mail twice a week. And we shall be only
happy to hear that nothing has happened. I can imagine that it is
hard for you to have strange children around you instead of Eva,
but in any rate she is safe in a friendly and carefree atmosphere.
My sister-in-law had her over weekend and wrote that she seems abso-
lutely happy there is great friend with Salmon's and has a number
of school friends. It was a great reassurance for me - and will be the
same to you - to hear that from a third person like my sister-in-law
who is more inclined to be critical and pessimistic than otherwise.
But she wrote that Eva could not be at a better place, and Salmon's
seem to do everything possible for her. - Excuse the hurry, the lecture is
at 5, it is now 3 and I have to post the letter before. Kisses to all L.

pages.transcription:
26. Oktober

Dear Manfred & Hannah, this only to tell you that we are
safely arrived in Buenos. Lotte was sufficiently exhausted
and we cant open 2 flower-shops with the flowers we found
in our apartement here. Then we went straight away {leerry}
behind all the people in the hall/ to the Opera where we had tickets for a
marvellous ballet and now I have to pay for all that with lectures in all
languages. The English, the Spanish are well arranged, but the great difficul[?]
by all the Jews. There are 250000 in this town and I have promised a
lecture for charity-purposes - now they fight, who shall arrange the lecture,
the Zionist, the refugees, the Spanioles and I have the secret hope, that
by this quarrel I shall escape, because they will not have finished the
discussions during my stay here. We go also to Cordoba, Rosario and
after that to Montevideo. The seven hours in the plane were a bit
shaky but we arrived without any trouble except that in the {20 minutes}
stay at Porto Alegre I could not get a coffee and smoke a cigare
because we had there a reception. In these countries a foreign writer
is still a rare and appreciated beast and the curiosity takes much of
our time, poor Lotte is hanging constantly on the phone and ex-
plaining in five different languages that we do not accept invitations.
All this will be over in a fortnight and then I am finally well a
month or six weeks before going for Newyork. We have no news
from Eva who will is not like to become ever a great writer but
I knew through my sister in law that she is happy and I wish
you could be with her. We speak every day how I regret it is that
you have to support all the difficulties - dont believe that we forget
you. For Freivental I have already tried something but it will
take some time. And poor Planker, - one cannot help him but we -
terially. Kindest regards to all from yours
Stefan Zweig

pages.transcription:
Buenos Aires, 27. 10. 40

Dear Hanna and Manfred,
We are now already a day in B-A. -
a new town, plenty of new people, plenty of telephone calls,
plenty of delegations who insist on some more gratis-lectures,
heaps of flowers, plenty of new things to eat, plenty of photos
and interviews; a funny sort of life for me, and at the same
time twenty times a day the thought: what is it like now in Eng-
land, what are they doing in this moment? I hope that this is
one of the rare weekends where Manfred is with you in
Bath and that Mama has left London. Lotte Sch[?] still is
at Raeburn's house and I again wrote her to address herself
to you if she needs something. - Between meeting people Stefan is
busy putting the finishing touch to his various lectures and
I am typing the last one. The Spanish lecture will be
"Unité spirituelle du monde", the English address will have
the cheering title "Hope in the Future" and the other charity
lecture will be about Vienna and its culture. Needless to
mention that every lecture means a cocktail party
before and a dinner party after. In a week's time we
leave for Cordoba, Rosario and Santa Fe who get a
Spanish lecture each - the one about spiritual Unity
and the other about Artistic Creation. This trip will take
about 5-6 days and will, I hope, be interesting as well
as entertaining. Mr. Cahn, Stefan's translator, will accom-
pany us (for his own pleasure, for our Spanish is, although
bad, sufficient to get along). About Uruguay we are Stefan has
suddenly decided to leave it out. It is a little out of the
way and he will have enough lecturing these two weeks
here. Perhaps we stay a few days longer here in Buenos
Aires and then return to Brazil where we will first try to
remain in Rio (but in a different hotel where we could have a
room with terrace which gives more air) and then, when it gets too hot,
go up to a place in the mountains, we do not yet know which.
Kindest regards and kisses, keep well
Lotte.

c/o Editora Guanabara
32 Rua Ouvidor, Rio

Buenos Aires, 1.11.40

Dear Hanna and Manfred, enclosed a long letter for Mama
which you please forward and which tells you nearly all
the news. I got your letter, Hanna, with Mama's, dated 5th Oct,
posted Bath 16th and forwarded from Rio, already
yesterday - it could hardly have been quicker. But you write
something about a letter which Manfred wrote; it was not inside, and we have
not had a letter from him for a long time. I can easily understand that
she lost a number of his patients in the last months, but why does 'nt he
come and stay with you completely, is this not possible? It would seem so
much more natural than to give up the rest of your house and move still
further into town. I am glad that Mama is now with her sisters, it will be one
worry less for you and Manfred. I am sorry that professor M. and his wife had
to leave you and I can only hope that the new solution works out sa-
tisfactorily and wish for you that your maid could join you in Bath so
that you had less work. I thought, Clara Jozs and Barbara were coming - how
did you get Erwin instead? Perhaps it is the better thing because I remember
that he was a clever little boy, and I hope he does not bother you by
being religious, and helps you instead in house and garden. If you
still convert the stables into living rooms - I thought Mr. Orchard wanted
to keep a cow in them - and take more children, you must beware of not
becoming a second Mrs. Levin. But if it is not too much for you -
for us it is a good thought that our house is being useful
at least and I am glad that Mr. Miller is able to work again - give
him our kindest regards as well as to Mr. Ingram and Mr. Orchard.
From Eva and Salmon's you have apparently had good news since your last
letter and from what my sister-in-law writes you can be com-
pletely reassured about her. She has had Eva for a weekend, she
saw Mr. Salmon and phones to Eva every week and she wrote that
there was no doubt that Eva was happy there, that she had a lot
of friends already and that Salmon's like her very much. If they
don't write often, it does not mean anything. They are very American,
kind, gay and without any imagination beyond their own scope, and
as somehow the life of the average American is always a rush they
probably do not realize that a child's letter is not enough for parents.
But I can absolutely rely upon my sister-in-law who is rather inclined
to critisize, that she immediately informs me if anything goes wrong, but
so far she wrote completely satisfied. - I shall write once more from here
before we leave for the provinces and I can only wish that you and
Manfred shall have no major troubles in the times to come.
Kindest regards and kisses, Lotte.

pages.transcription:
Buenos Aires, 9. 11. 40

Dear Mama, Hanna & Manfred,
Only a short letter today, for although I
did not accompany Stefan to his lectures in Cordoba
Santa Fé and Rosario - from where he will return to-morrow -
I have been rather busy, getting visas, tickets etc. of all kinds,
answering the letters and the telephone, being invited although
alone and getting rid of a cold. Stefan is still away and will
return to-morrow about lunchtime. At 6 we have promised to go
once more to the Opera to see a ballett and Hansel & Gretel,
arranged by old friends from Salzburg, at 10 two men are coming
who want to see him about something, Monday he has a lecture
at La Plata, one hour from here, Tuesday he has to see a doctor
who wants to clean his ears (nothing more, only that hurt a little)
Wednesday we fly over to Montevideo where we will be received,
offered lunch and a reception after the lecture and a short
radio talk, Thursday afternoon we will be back here, in
the evening while I pack Stefan will give a radio talk
here, and Friday at 6 in the morning we leave for Rio
where we hope to arrive in the afternoon. In Rio we
will go to another hotel this time, where we get a room
in the 6th floor with a large covered balcony so
that it is cooler and more agreable. There we will stay
until it becomes too hot and then either go directly
to the States or somewhere in the mountains near Rio -
we have not yet decided which. In any case we hope
to visit Eva by the beginning of the new year at
the latest. I have regular reports through my sister-
in-law who had her for the weekend once, phones
every week and in her last letter wrote that she was
going to visit her shortly. From her I hear that Eva is
well and happy at Salmon's. Eva herself does appa-
rently like writing as little as ever, and I am afraid
Salmon's are not any better in this respect. But you know
pages.notes: Brief auf Hotelpapier (City Hotel, Buenos Aires). Handschrift in blauer Tinte.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
from Manfreds example that an active dislike
for writing does not mean a bad character, and
I am sure the same is the case with Salmon's.
We shall not be sorry to leave and look
forward to returning to Rio - although our joy is rather
spoiled by the sudden death {tragic} of a stupid and unhovat[?] 
accident of our best friend there, Hernandez Cata,
minister of Cuba, who in this short time had become
one of our closest friends. - Here we have had a hectic
time and did not like it too much in spite of the
wonderful reception Stefan has had and which sur-
passed even that of Rio. But we prefer the Brazilians
and the beautiful landscape of Rio, and maybe for
that reasons our impressions were somewhat biassed
and prejudiced.
I do hope from all my heart that
you all are well and it is a relief to read in the
papers that the attacks on London are diminishing
in force. Let us hope that they will soon be
stopped altogether. Also here we have found a
spontaneous pro-British sympathy.
Kindest regards and kisses,
also Manfred included,
Lotte.

pages.transcription:
12. Nov. 1940
Dear Hannah, I did send you today a cable asking
for you to inform Friedental that I was informed today
that the Argentine ~~Consulate~~ {in London} has been instructed to
deliver a visa for him. I was here in private audience at the minister
of the Exterior Roca to ask him for three visas, one for Friedental
and he was so kind to grant it to me and as his secretary told me the
cables have gone already to London. Please help him with money for
the passage and as much as he wants; here in Buenos Aires I have
instructed my friends to be useful to him and also in Brazil he can
have opportunities. For the United States I could not help him for the
moment.
I have just returned from the tour in the province
which was as strenuous as successful - I am glad Lotte remained
in Buenos Aires, she would not have stood this strain, lectures, nights
in the train, and drives from 7 in the morning, receptions, photographs.
It was a sort of sensation, an author of Europe who speaks Spanish
and now it goes to Montevideo where I have to speak in a hall be-
fore 4000 - 5000 people, leaving behind our flowergarden - even
the W.C and the bidet are full of flowers for Lotte. But how happy
we shall be to have again a quiet life and not to rivalise with
cinema-stars. We have refused, Chile, Paraguay, Colombia, Cuba, we
have enough for the moment - enough of success, fees, flowers,
people and refugees. How we are longing to sit quietly again in
Bath!
A sad news was that our best friend in Rio, Hernandez Catá
pages.notes: Brief auf Hotelpapier (City Hotel, Buenos Aires). Handschrift in violetter Tinte. Die Seite endet mitten im Satz.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, leer.

pages.transcription:
The ambassador of Cuba has been killed in an stupid
aeroplan-accident. Three days after his death a letter
of him ~~reaches~~ {would} me here, saying, that he wait with his
carf on the aerodrom, when we arrive - and he lost his
life meanwhile in a plane excursion. He was the kindest man
I have met since years and he guaranties for Friedental in
Cuba - I hope they did send the visa to Friedental from Ha-
vanna. You understand that the only way to be grateful for
the preference and happiness which we enjoy is that we try to
use here our influence to help to others. It is frightfully
difficult for there exits a secret order not to give any more
visas to Jews and only the minister of the Exterior could
personally break this iron rule. What times, - and how
often, you can not imagine to go our thoughts to you and
what we have too much of happiness here would be due
to you all. Now I have to work for two month on my book
on Brazil and then we will think over if we go to Newyork
- my sister in law is in contact with Eva and we get always
notices through her - not from Eva herself, who seems to be
too happy to write. Yours

Stefan Zweig
My dears, I am terribly busy, tired and still upset
about the news of the death of Catá, and that is the
only thing which spoils the pleasure of returning to
Rio to a normal working life and a beautiful landscape.
I shall write you at length immediately we arrive in Rio.
In the meantime kindest regards and kisses
Lotte

Rückseite des zweiten Blattes, leer.

pages.transcription:
on the way from Buenos Aires to Rio 15. Nov. Dear Hannah and Manfred, now in the
aeroplane we have the first moment since three weeks. The strain was large, yesterday
at 10 30 I read still broadcast, we came home at midnight where a cinema agent was waiting for me.
In the morning at 5 we had to get up and found at six the same agent waiting, now we are
on the way, after being ~~photographed~~ {been} for the thousands and last time. I had altogether ten
lectures instead of four in these three weeks and we have doubled the fees of the last ones
except the one in English and one in German I gave for charity purposes. And then the table
needs, the interviews, the cinephotos, the travels - I have at least made the tour round the
world - yesterday still Uruguay, going and returning by plane: poor Lotte was frightfully
tired even without having accompanied me in the most strenuous voyages in the province.
But now it is over. I have earned enough in these three hard weeks that we can now pass
the next three month in our modest way and do some work. I am longing to have some
quiet time without publicity. And whenever I want to take up again the lecturing
I can do it, I have invitations to Paraguay, Cuba, Columbia, Chile and I do not know
how many countries and of course here and in Uruguay again. But we will stay for
two months at least in Brasil and see how we can stand the climate in summer, pro-
bably we shall retire in the mountains (the only difficulty is to find a hotel there with
a little comfort and quietness, as all Rio moves at the same time to these places)
As to Freivental I wrote you, that I had a private audience at the Minister of
Foreign Affairs who at my request granted me three visas, two for my former pub-
lishers in Holland and one for Freivental; as I hear the cables have gone already to
the respective consulates. I am nevertheless not quite sure, that all will go smoothly
as every time we ourselves had to do with visas there were always delays and
something forgotten; if it should not be delivered to him, please cable that I may
remind here. I remember how complicated it was to transform our visitors visa
to Brasil in a permanent one and you may imagine that all was well prepared for
us, but always there is something forgotten or a detail wanting in these bureaucratic
times; now all is in perfect order for us and we want no more special permissions
to go in and out of Brasil and can ever stay as long as we want
All what you write about our house in Bath is very reconforting; please do not forget
that you can make me personally a great pleasure and that is in disposing of all
my belongings for you and your family as if it were yours. It is a great satis-
faction for me to know that it is useful to somebody - and especially to people
like you - while it is totally useless to me. Please remember this always. And
Manfred shall have from time to time a rest. Who knows what is expecting still us all
and only one thing is really wise for the future - to keep fit, to have his body and
his brains in good order. As to Eidamaca I am afraid that the death of our
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf gelbem Papier. Die Tinte ist violett. Die Zeilen sind eng geschrieben.
Rückseite der ersten Seite, leer.

pages.transcription:
from Hernandez Cata will prove fatal to his Cuban visa as it was
Cata who gave the garanties for him and now the only man who could urge if there
was some hindrance or delay, is gone. I am so sorry for Eisemann that it did
not work immediately as Cata and I had hoped, but perhaps there will be another
opportunity. A bookseller of Buenos Aires wired him for books and they are already
in touch - here is a lot of wealth but the people in Argentine have not yet learned
to spend it in cultural things, they begin now smoothly. The country is not very inspi-
ring and both Lotte and I prefer Brasil which is picturesk and has a great charm
in the landscape and in the people. I hope you will know it a day. And now I leave
the sheet to Lotte, who is again allright and will write you all I have forgotten
to tell you about Argentine and Uruguay (where the abundance of food and the
quietness of life has for us Europeans somewhat exciting) Yours Stefan
Dear Hanna and Manfred, We received yesterday both Hanna's letter with the copy of
Eva's first letter and yours, Manfred which was very interesting. I am happy and
grateful to know her safe and well, and if she does not like my family-
in-law, she exaggerates perhaps but is not altogether wrong. I was glad
to know that you were both all-right so far, but I would feel better
if you were both away from London. When do you give up Woodstock Road?
- We are glad to return to Rio and we are determined to live quietly there
and to work. I am only sorry that I did not bring a new Royal Portable Typewriter
with me, mine is beginning to wear out, although still incomparably better than
your brother's. Has Heiner got all the papers for the affidavit now? You did not
mention it and I only had information from Newyork that he had send a cable
confirming the receipt of the affidavit and that the forms had been sent by registered
airmail from Buenos Aires. Stefan's first wife and most of his colleagues have been able
to get out of France and are now in Newyork. In South Am. there are few newcomers
as visas to all the countries are almost impossible to get. About our journey to
Argentine I shall write more later on when my impressions have settled down. For the
moment I only remember the meat portions were enormous, the weather
continually changing from hot to cold, the telephone continually ringing,
Stefan giving one lecture after the other and little speeches in between,
myself continually dead-tired and our time taken by all sorts of things
from early morning to late at night. From Uruguay my principal impressions
were the first flight by hydro-avion and the fact that we did not speak
anything but Spanish and that fortunately ladies were excluded from the
banquet after the lecture. Best wishes and kisses and kindest regards
to the Rosemount - and Woodstock inhabitants Lotte

Rückseite der dritten Seite, leer.

pages.transcription:
Rio, 19.11.40
Dear Hanna & Manfred, My sister-in-law's letter
about reading Eva's letter where she says that she did
not like it in her house, will have reached you be-
fore this one and I hope you don't take it seriously.
It is a stupid incident but without importance and it shows Eva's
childishness that she gave this letter - yes! - to my sister-in-law to
post it. The important thing is that she writes to you regularly,
for Salmon's seem to be in that respect like all our American
friends none of whom writes us a word, although definitely people like
Huebsch and Rose are good friends. They have not yet realised what letters
can mean to those far away. To me letters mean [?] and so please write, write many and long letters until finally the
personal contact can be reestablished. Kindest regards and best love
Lotte

Dear A. & M. we cannot tell you anything about Eva, as she did not
write to us - I have the feeling that the Helaus[?] like to keep her for
themselves and do nothing to keep her in touch with her family
Eva will perhaps have to fight to get her back from her new parents.
Anyhow we hope to see her in February. For the moment we have but
one desire: To sit quietly and not to move. I have done enough with
travelling by air and auto and trains and hydroplanes in those 16
days - more than another in a lifetime and the idea to travel
14 days to New York is for the moment a ghastly one for me. I am
very worried about Manfred. I do not understand why he must
just now start a new profession as a Xray specialist - after
the war his practice will flourish again and he would better do
to take a rest. Dont think too much about the future and remem-
ber always that you have a child who wants you. Dont worry
about money, you should know already that one of the very few
pleasures I have now{left} is to know that you have not to think about
and may freely and largely dispose of all I have - we have a
duty one against the other in such times. I told you that I had
to give ten lectures instead of four and am invited to give
more in Danish and in all possible countries of South America
- so we have at least something useful to do and I am glad that
I am physically able to assist stand the great
strain. Ever yours Stefan Zweig

pages.transcription:
Rio, Central Hôtel
Rio, 22.11.40
Dear Hanna & Manfred, Just now your telegram about the new
address - I am happy to know you well but rather angry about
Salmon's thoughtlessness not to see that the child writes re-
gularly and glad to know that a letter of Eva's must reach you
one of these days, sent by my sister-in-law with her explanation
about reading Eva's letter. We have also had no direct news from
her and it is fortunate that my sister-in-law kept me in-
formed and that I always wrote you her impressions. - About the
new living arrangement of Manfred's I send my best wishes,
all included in the one that he may be able to live there for
the duration without having to change, and that he can keep up
quiet long weekends at Bath. - About E's visa we cabled you
again yesterday. The explanation is that the second person for whom
Stefan had also secured (or thought to have secured) a visa to Argentine
from England, had cabled about difficulties in getting it in spite
of telegraphic instructions from Buenos Aires, and that led to the
second cable from there, ordering the Arg. consul in London to
give at least a tourist visa to those two. But maybe Fr.
owing to his protestant faith had less difficulties than the
other, the former editor of Cherido in Amsterdam who is now in
England. You did not write anything about your brother, so I
am afraid it is not yet settled. Tell him, if he likes to
take Stefan's manuscript case for the journey. It is always useful
and I am sorry I did not insist on taking it. - Our plans keep
on changing. The newest idea is to stay here in Rio until
the end of January and then go to USA for 3 months in-
stead of packing up again in a few weeks to go to the mountains.
Until now it is not at all hot in spite of splendid weather. Ste-
fan wants me to apologise to Mama because I wrote her that
it is now the rainy season - we have a large room with a big
covered terrace and no sun after 10 a.m., overlooking the bay and
catching every breeze of air, looking down directly on a bathing
beach, and the room even has a real writing-table. So I think we
shall stay here and see how long we like it. If it gets very hot

2) in the end, we think of going to USA, stopping first in Bahia and
Pernambuco, then take a boat to New Orleans and from there con-
tinue by train to Newyork, where we would look for a hotel or
small furnished service flat somewhere near the town but not in
the town itself, as there are too many friends and collegues
of Stefan's now in Newyork to allow him quiet working hours.

detailed reports, but I am convinced already now that she
feels very much at home at New Rochelle as I take her
silence for a sign of being pleasantly occupied all the time.
I suppose it will be by the end of Jan., middle of Febr. that
we get to Newyork. - I hope that in Bath all goes smoothly in
spite of the many people and that none of the children or adults gives
you any trouble. Please tell Lizzy and Mannheims that for a long
time I intended to write them and that I have not given up the idea.
- It will soon be time to congratulate you and Mama to your
birthdays. I am sorry I cannot send any presents, I can only say

for yourself or for each other in my name.

and kisses, wishes and best love,

pages.transcription:
Hotel Central
Rio, 3.12.40

Dear Hanna u Manfred, No letter from you or Mama since
more than 2 weeks, and I am glad we had at least your cable.
But I do not want to wait longer, as this letter shall convey
to you, Hanna, our heartiest congratulations and best wishes for
your birthday, and many happy returns; let us hope the next will
see us all united again. I cabled you that at least one letter of
Eva was on the way and that we had one. She seems to be quite
well and happy there, also my sister-in-law wrote lately that she
had again spoken to her on the phone, and if all goes according to
plan I hope to see her in February. In the meantime we are
trying out the Brazilian summer. It is gradually getting warmer, but
our room is very airy, Stefan, as you know, enjoys perspiration, and
so all is well so far - and we often try to imagine your life
which in every respect must be the opposite to ours. I hope that
at least Manfred takes a long Christmas holiday at Bath although
I am not sure whether it is still as quiet as it was the last
months. Do all the families in Rosemount use the sitting-room? And
is Clara with child out there now? And how is life in Regent Lodge?
Was the removal difficult or did'nt you take your furniture there?
Marta will be busy there, I suppose, and glad of it. I do not know
whether I wish your brothers things were settled or not, I would dislike
the idea of his travelling now. Paul, contrary to your letters has
not yet arrived and Stefan is glad about it. We lead a very quiet
life now. As long as the family of our friend Catá who died in that
stupid accident, was still in Rio we were kept busy visiting them
and Stefan spoke at a commemoration. Now they have left and we
see few people, do not go out much, but sit on our balcony and
work and read. We have made one or two more excursions and are
always delighted to discover still more and more unknown things.
Once more many happy returns, and best wishes, Lotte.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Sehr gut lesbar.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer.

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, latest wishes for your birthday; my own was somewhat
spoiled; ~~at~~ at one of the numerous registrations a nice, half-coloured girl,
His charming type I admire so much, wrote in the register under hair; 'grey'
As I said it was the first time in my life she was so kind to alter it into
brown, but I am afraid, it was the last time. Do not follow this bad example
You can imagine how we read the newspapers - with all your feelings
and you know how hopeful I was from the first day; we try to imagine all
our friends and where they may be. I have myself no news and do not know
where to write, as most of them have without any doubt left London. Often
- no, daily we are ashamed to enjoy such a glorious summer here, the
heat is not so great as we feared and we hope to stand it through. I am
glad to have a rest from my lectures, I hate to be from morning to evening
a public person and enjoy now our privacy. We have only one room here
but with a very big terrace so that it makes nearly two - what I miss are
books as I cannot store them here. Of that I will shall have enough in the
States with her marvellous libraries - I dream to go to a place (Uni-
versity or other town) about two hours from New York to have a quiet life
and notwithstanding the torribly to, a go to town - about the distance
of Bath to London, which was so agreeable in peace time. So Lotte could see
from time to time Eva and [my] brother and a few of the friend, but I
have to avoid the innumerables which are now there. How much will you
have to tell us, I do really not know how you divide your life between
all those who want your care and your help, but above you have to len
you will be anxious about Eva who really seems to enjoy her new life
and even our rather harsh letter, that she may write you at least once a
week, will not spoil her the privileged stay. I think we better direct the last
letter to Bath as I hope from all my heart that Manfred will take there
a holiday; one must nowadays seize every good moment and enjoy it -
let us not think too much, it doesnt help. Give my love to your sister, to all
our friends if you see them - I wont like you to describe how peaceful
and even without any imagination of all our fate this southamerican
world is but you would not believe it. Yours ever
Stefan Zweig

pages.transcription:
7 XII 1940 Dear Hannah and Manfred, we have a letter from
Eva today that she has for 4 weeks no news from you, I am afraid
that letters have been lost. We wrote to you both every week regularly
and now being anxious we have tried to make an arrangement with
the Western Telegraf that all the telegramms we send could be paid by
you as we want to inform you regularly about your daughter and
are somewhat short of money. You will understand that and I hope it
will be possible so that you may not have to add your other anxious
fimes the worry about your child. Please send us like before cables
from time to time - we are in such an enormous distance that letters
are not sufficient as they seem to take much time. Eva writes quite
happy, she is somewhat disappointed that we arrive later than we
proposed but I want badly a few weeks without travelling. From us
there is nothing new to relate. We live a retired life and till now
we could stand the heat very well, only one wants more sleep and
feels his energy a little diminished. We our selves have no letters from
you all now for three weeks but your cable reassured us at least
that you are allright. Kindest regards to all and love to you
Rio, Hotel Central. Stefan Zweig

Dear Hanna & Manfred, - There seems to be an all-round
shortage of letters just now - we have no letters from you since
3 weeks you have no letter from Eva for 5 weeks and she has no
letter from you since 4 weeks. But I hope that all these letters
which certainly have been written are not lost but only de-
layed and will arrive as a nice Christmas surprise. In any
case I repeat our birthday wishes which we expressed in our last
letter. - We are all-right, it is not yet so very hot and I
have not even started bathing. We are continuing to work.
and to see few people, and my only activity consists in
taking Spanish lessons, in order to change my Esperanto
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf gelblichem Papier. Die erste Seite enthält zwei Abschnitte, der zweite beginnt nach dem Absatz.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, leer.

pages.transcription:
2)
into real Spanish. From Eva we had another letter
to-day telling that she has seen Rose Wohl and her sister and
brother-in-law and that they are "very sweet". But I have
had no word from Rose herself - it seems to be a general
defect of the American character, this not-writing - although I
feel sure of her friendship and very best intentions. Only my
sister-in-law is reliable and I am beginning to appreciate
it very much. She wrote a few days ago that she had again
spoken to Eva by phone and that everything was allright
and that she was going to see her soon. I am looking forward
to seeing Eva in February. Even if we do not remain in
Newyork, we will not be more than two hours away at the
most, and I shall be able to see her frequently for at
least 2 or 3 months. To make plans or even to think ahead
for more than 4 or 5 months one does not dare although I
always hope for pleasant events and sometimes even have
rather premature dreams about being at home again with you.
I am surprised to find myself so much more sentimental
than I thought, but I discover more and more how deeply
this habit of living with you for so long, has grown and how
much I miss you. My only consolation is that at least
our house is useful to you as a place for rest and I
do wish it will remain it. How are Raumann fitting
in that Rosemount-life? Give them my kindest regards,
also to all the others especially to Livy and Ursula
to whom I want to write since a long time.
Best wishes, kisses and souvenirs,
Lotte

pages.transcription:
Rio, 11.12.40
Dear Martha, It is a long time since I want to address
you again a few personal words, only there is usually a rush
on the days where letters have to be posted-and first of all written.
I very much hope that you are well and I even suppose
that for you the removal to another flat together with Smolletts
is rather welcome than otherwise. I can imagine that nearly
as lively as „Rosemount“, even if there are few visitors.
That Lotte is representing you in Bath I know and I hope she
likes being there as much as you and I loved it. But where
is Raethe now, could she continue work in that children's
home at Uxbridge? And did you get any good news about
the girls' brother? I do hope you did. I often think of our
house how it is now, without you, without Eva, without us and
on hot days I remember the wintry afternoons when we came
up from the town and gathered round the fire. I don't know
whether I am getting old, but I certainly got sentimental about
Bath and the years in Woodstock Road. The house in Woodstock
Road seems over now, but I hope that one day we will all
unite again in „Rosemount“. - In the meantime we are braving
the heat which is slowly developping, and I have even de-
cided to go and bathe in the sea to-morrow morning at
8! (later it gets too hot). We intend to remain here another
month and then hope to go to the States for a few winter
months. I am looking forward to seeing ~~eva~~ Eva who seems
to be so busy going to parties that she has to be reminded
of letter-writing.
With the best wishes for the New Year
Dear Martha, Lotte as a worthy aunt of Eva has left Lotte.
this letter a good fortnight on her desk and so it arrives after
Christmas and Newyear. When shall we meet again. I am longing
after the „Heimstätte Marthas“ and an own room with my books
and not more to see luggage, visas, railways for some time. Yours Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig auf gelblichem Papier. Die letzte Zeile 'Lotte.' ist eine handschriftliche Ergänzung von Lotte Zweig.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer.

pages.transcription:
Rio, 11.12.40
Dear Hanna + Manfred, Finally we had a letter from
you after more than 3 weeks without mail. In the meantime
you seem to have moved into your new flat, and I hope
you can stay there as long as you like. What did you do with
your maid, could you take her to Bath? Whom are you going
to take instead of Mrs Youngman and her children? I am
very glad, Hanna, that you wrote about yourselves, because I
want to know as much as possible about your life, and
there are still lots of questions which I could put you. For
instance, who is Frank? I thought you had Erwin there and I
cannot think of any Frank I know. From your brother we had a
letter, thanking us, but I hope he does not travel now
during the cold season, should he go, one of Stefan's tweed
suits might be useful. - As to my dear Brother's letter: help
him with money if you think he needs it and as you say
yourself, he might be really at the end of his ressources.
As to the Brazilian visa, I do not think it will be possible. As
they do not give visas now as a rule it would mean giving a
personal guarantee and that is the only thing I cannot ask of
Stefan in this case. I shall write him next week, should you
see him before tell him we think it over and give him
something if you think he needs it. I think I shall also write
to mama, and don't you worry too much about it. I know
what it means beginning to help him, but we were not sus-
prised - it had to come one day. - Forgive if I do not
write more to-day, it is already late for posting, and
it is hot. I hope for a thunderstorm to-night and
then I shall write more at length. Keep well and
induce Manfred to stay as long as possible with you
in Bath.
Yours Lotte.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Die Zeile 'of 6.11.' wurde oben rechts nachträglich eingefügt. Die Tinte ist violett.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
I join a few lines on this famous paper which would be more
convenient for other purposes. Rio is and will always remain
the most beautiful town of the world, even such a
uncnthusiastic being as Lotte finds it wonderful. All would be
ideal here without the heat {in summer} as there are already flats with
aircooling I think it over if it should be necessary for my health
to go to a southern climat. And how far is this world from
from America! One can write only by air mail
and that won't mean for me never to send manuscripts
and for Lotte to write still shorter letters than usual. My Spanish
makes good progress and I like the language enormously - the
easiest perhaps of all Latin ones and I wonder what they will
say in Buenos Aires when I am lecturing in Spanish.
Here we live a very quiet live, I do my best to continue
this retirement after having seen so many people and if
I am giving a lecture I will do it on the last days. I
have not heard a word from Europe since months ex-
cept your letters and also from America I hear nearly
nothing, but I do not complain, all personal things
being quite indifferent now. For Friedental I can
do nothing from here except if he would like to live
here, all correspondence has no effect in America, one
has to phone and phone every day and to run. A few
weeks ago it would have been much easier, but he never
mentioned his intention. Thanks for all Stefan Zweig

Rückseite des zweiten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
11. XII. Dear Hannah, we have today a card of my sister in law who
was visiting Eva - I must admit that she takes it seriously and is
already affected with all the responsibility-complex of the Zweigs.
In this case it is very good and you can rely upon her better than
on others. Dont worry if there come no letters regularly; we also got
~~yours~~ with a long delay. - We do not know exactly when to go and
How, firstly we want to {combine} it with a trip to Bahia and
the Northern Brazil, which would pay us half the fare and the
fares for the enormous distances are frightfully high. The disa-
greeable thing is that you have to book three weeks before as there
are few planes and we have {no} ship from the North of Brazil
on the other hand I want to finish first a little book on Brazil,
which will be very helpful to us and perhaps to others in the
future. We are now in plain summer, but I find the heat still
tolerable, only you want more sleep and eat less, what is per-
haps an advantage for my {counterpoint}. Now to you. I implore you
again and again, write freely and without scruples of all
I have, help your family and also your brother as I believe
that there is very little chance to get him now a visa. I have al-
ways tried my best {for others} and I hope, that Catas daughter will now see
in Cuba for Eismann after the death of her father - Here we
are in a particular situation because we have here the personal
responsibility for any person we would try to get over and we
know how small the chances are for a newcomer. As to Victor
I wrote him but has no reply, give Kocher and all others my
kindest regards, we must try for Hermann Neisse all immediately
in the States. In no case we shall stay in Newyork, I have to work
and could not have a quiet life there - probably we go somewhere
to a small university or near town {to be} that we could come from time
to time. All is so very obscure in those times - as to you I repeat,
do not worry about the material side of things and try to keep yourself
[Randnotiz links:] P.S. I hope you will stay the whole Christmas time in Bath and [?] Stanford
and you would not return to London but after a good rest. Yours Stefan Zweig

pages.transcription:
Hotel Central                                     Rio, 15.12.40

Dear Hanna & Manfred, Just a few lines to-day to tell
you that we remember you and hope that you are well. We
are beginning to feel rather warm, and go out little and work
a lot instead. I have begun bathing and shall make it a habit
to do so every morning before breakfast. At night it is good to
be with friends who have a car to take us a little further out-
20 minutes from here it is already much cooler and refreshing.
In January I suppose we will still go to the north of Brasil,
to Bahia, Recife and Belem and from there probably continue
to U.S.A. - we may decide to fly as Belem is already a third
of the whole distance and there is no connection by boat to
Newyork. - I hope you have had a very quiet and restful
Christmas and that Manfred spent already the your birthday
in Bath and remained until after New Year.
Kindest regards, kisses, best wishes, yours, Lotte

Dear Hannah and Manfred, there is not much to tell about
us. We support the heat better than we supposed and I con-
tinue to work regularly but without enthusiasm (for
whom does one write to day?) We have no news from all
our friends and are glad to be in touch with you. As to
our voyage we do not enjoy it to much, we would like
to have a few month without packing and wandering
around, but who has not this wish to have a quiet life
in these terrible times and we all must learn to dream
of things which once were the most natural. But let us
keep firm. We are with you with all our thoughts and
loves                                                              Stefan

Hotel Central
Rio, 16.12.40
Dear Hanna, This morning I got your letter (N°1 to Rio) from Nov.16th as
well as one from mama. In the meantime you will have had letters from
us and I hope long ones. We will be there in February and then I will tell
you all I can about her and her life. I wrote to Salmon's about a fortnight
ago a very friendly and polite letter asking them to see to it that Eva
writes regularly and explaining what it means for parents to be without
news. The Americans have not much imagination, and also my friend Roze whom
Eva visited weeks ago, has not written me a single line although she should know
that I would be glad to have a report about the child. Meanwhile we had a Christmas
card from Eva together with my sister-in-law who has visited her again and who
writes that everything is all-right. I am very glad your brother does not have to
travel now, it is the word[?] possible season now. About Ursula's future it seems to
early yet to worry. I suppose the best will be if her parents keep her with
them later, even if her mother should go out to work, she could do part of
the household, and as the public schools are free & Eva is visiting one &
in some districts very good, that should be no problem. Should we
be in USA when they arrive - I don't think that they will be able to
travel before several months - we will of course advise them as much as
we can, and even should we have left, I would try and recommend
Heiner as well as Alice to people which I think might be useful to
them. You will have moved into your new flat now, I suppose, and be
very glad to be settled again. Did you get part of the furniture to Bath al-
ready? You are quite right in all you do to improve the house and I wish
Manfred would frequent it even more. A pity he has to take that X-Ray course
in London. I am glad that you have Ranmans with you and that you get on
so well together. Give them my kindest regards. - Here is great joy everywhere
about the success of the Greek and of the English offensive, and the great
number of jokes that are in circulation about the Italians, is a good
expression of this state of mind - Who are the fastest runners in the world?.
The Greek, because they even catch up with the Italians. - The Italian colony
in Sao Paulo is supposed to have asked for police protection because two
Greets have landed in Santos. - A man orders spaghetti in a restaurant and
when he gets them asks for English Worcester sauce. When the sauce is brought,
the spaghetti have disappeared, - etc .etc.

pages.transcription:
2) The other day you asked how we get along with our things. As a
matter of fact, I had often been on the point of writing about it,
but at the last moment I always thought - I cannot write you
about such ridiculous things now, you would not be in the mood
for it. Stefan had a second tropical suit made and always wears
one while the other is being cleaned. The tails he did not need yet.
The invitations, although numerous and often big receptions, were
ever so formal and smoking and evening dress we have at only
worn once on the boat and once in Rio. I had to buy 3 more
summer dresses, washable simple things, and for invitations I wore
alternatively all my black dresses, and the dresses I bought in Poland
years ago, did very good service. For afternoon receptions - if the day was
a little cool, I used my black woollen dresses, the one from Poland
or the one from May Fair which I bought last year.
And as the invitations were at so many different places, I got round
beautifully. Black is the great fashion this year - in Newyork even
for summer wear, ridiculous as it looked in the hot streets - and the
materials of my dresses in wool as well as silk is so much su-
perior to all what you get here that I was quite well dressed as
a rule. Now the mania of invitations has died down somewhat.
The heat makes the people inactive and lazy, and most families
are preparing to leave for the summer. We stand the heat very
well so far although at times one gets a little fed up with it.
But as the picture houses and casinos are air-conditioned and the sea
is near, one can always get some fresh and cool air, and in the
own room one dresses not much better than Adam and Eve and
gets refreshment from the douche and the ventilator. - You will have
got an enquiry from the Western Cables whether you are willing to pay
for our telegrams and I am glad you said you would. I think it is
less trouble for you that way than sending reply paid. As to the title
so I will see whether I can send you a letter with certified signature,
otherwise an authorisation would have little value.
Kindest regards to you and Manfred, so also
and Ranmans and all the children,
Lotte

pages.transcription:
Copy of letter to Jan
Hotel Central                                Rio de Janeiro, 18.Dec. 1940.

Dear Jan,
I have received your letter of Nov. 8th and I have discussed
with Stefan all the questions it involves and immediately made enquiries.
The information which I got from the most competent sources is
that unfortunately there are no chances for a Brazilian visa at the mo-
ment. Besides the capitalist visa - which is out of question as a sum
of ten thousand dollars has to be brought to Brasil - and apart from the
question of the religion they issue now only a few visas for special
technicians and agriculturists which are needed by the Government. -
As to other South American countries, the regulations may vary a little,
but we know from our enquiries for friends that the difficulties as just
as great - for all these countries have now the principle rather to ~~to~~
prevent than to allow immigration. Should the situation change, I would
of course let you know it immediately.
As to financial assistance in the case of your emigration, I
must tell you already now that it is unfortunately impossible for us
to help anybody outside of England, as we have had to leave everything
behind and ourselves living from month to month and from country to
country (we are leaving Brazil in January). In England, however, Stefan
has left with Hanna a certain amount for current expenses in Bath and for
unforeseen payments, and he is writing her not to let you get into
distress.
I can well understand how unhappy you must feel in your present
situation, separated from your wife and unable to find a position, and
I am sorry that there is at present no chance to help you to emigrate
to another counrty. I hope at least that you have good news from your
wife who at any rate is safe from bombing attacks and that you per-
sonally do not suffer too much from the effects of the war. - As to
the past, do not let us talk about it any more, there is for every one
of us plenty to worry about the present time and the future.

With best wishes for the new year and kindest regards,

Dear Hannah, Lotte shows me this letter to her brother. I leave
it quite to you how much you think necessary or advisable
to let him have at once. Only please tell him that this
means no permanent obligation of {our} ~~their~~ part. Any help out
of England is thoroughly excluded as we have ourselves to
renew from month to month our life. [Unterschrift: Stefan]

pages.transcription:
Stefan Zweig

RIO, ANO NOVO 1941

No mar, tanta tormenta e tanto damno;
Tantas vezes a morte apercebida!
Na terra, tanta guerra, tanto engano,
Tanta necessidade aborrecida!
Onde pode acolher-se um fraco humano?!
Onde terá segura a curta vida,
Que não se arme e se indigne o céu sereno
Contra um bicho da terra tão pequeno?!

Camões, LUSIADAS C. I., E. CVI

____________________

Weh, wieviel Not und Fährnis auf dem Meere
Wie nah der Tod in tausendfalt Gestalten!
Auf Erden wieviel Krieg! Wieviel der Ehre
Verhasst Geschäft! Ach dass nur eine Falte
Des Weltballs für den Menschen sicher wäre,
Sein bischen Dasein friedlich durchzuhalten,
Indes die Himmel wetteifern im Sturm.
Und gegen wen? Den schwachen Erdenwurm!

Trad. STEFAN ZWEIG.
pages.notes: Vorderseite der Postkarte. Gedruckter Text mit handschriftlicher Signatur 'Stefan Zweig' am oberen Rand.

pages.transcription:
Thanks for your cable!

I have letters from Friedental, I seems that the poor fellow has a
hard life and as he is merely too proud to ask for help I would like
to ask you to help him substantially; perhaps he could go to the country
and finish his book. Also to Felix Braun 9 Castle Crescent, Kendal,
Westmoreland help would be welcome; he lives with his old mother
there and his sister. Victor has had a new operation, his will to
see his wife in South Africa keeps him alive. I will try to send
them a small food parcel only it is not so easy and we have no
news that a single of those we did send has arrived. I hope you
will both soon enjoy the garden and the well merited holidays
Yours
Stefan
